# A SUMMARY OF THE WHOLE
## HOLY SCRIPTURE,
### NAMELY, OF THE BOOKS OF THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'D' depicting a biblical scene, likely King David kneeling in prayer in a landscape with his harp beside him.</image-desc>

<margin>
Genesis 1.
Genesis 2.
</margin>
The books of the Old Testament teach us that the God whom the Hebrews—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—worshiped is the only true God, almighty and eternal. Out of His own goodness, He created heaven and earth and everything within them by His Word. From Him all things proceed, and without Him nothing exists. He is just and merciful, working all things in everyone according to His own will; no one may ask Him why He acts in this way or that.

<margin>
Genesis 3.
</margin>
Furthermore, these books teach that this same God created Adam, the first man, in His own image and likeness, and appointed him master over all created things on earth. However, through the envy and deceit of the Devil, Adam disobeyed the command of his Creator. By his sin, he brought sin into this world—a sin so great that we, born of him according to the flesh, are by nature "children of wrath." Because of this, we are made subject to death, damnation, and the yoke and tyranny of the Devil.

<margin>
Genesis 22, 26, 28, 49.
Acts 13.
Isaiah 7, 9, 11.
Galatians 3.
Jeremiah 23, 33.
Ezekiel 34, 37.
Daniel 9.
Micah 5.
Zechariah 9.
</margin>
Nevertheless, God the Father promised that blessed "seed"—Jesus Christ His Son, our Savior—to Adam, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David, and the other Patriarchs. He was to be the one who would liberate from the tyranny of the Devil all those who believed in this promise with a living faith and trusted in Jesus Christ, hoping for liberation from Him and through Him. This promise is repeated very frequently throughout the books of the Old Testament.

<margin>
Romans 3.
Psalm 18.
Hebrews 10.
Colossians 2.
</margin>
In the meantime, while the promised salvation and liberation were being awaited by the Patriarchs, human nature was so proud and corrupt that men would not willingly acknowledge themselves as sinners in need of a promised Savior. Therefore, the Law was given by God through Moses, written on stone tablets. Its purpose was that through the Law, sin and the malice of the human heart might be recognized, making men thirst more ardently for the coming of Christ, who would redeem them from their sins—something that animal sacrifices and offerings could not achieve. Those rituals were merely shadows and figures <note>In early Christian theology, "shadows and figures" (types) were Old Testament events or rituals seen as symbolic precursors to the life of Jesus.</note> of the true offering of Christ, by which all sins were to be erased and abolished.

<margin>
John 1.
Romans 5, 8.
Galatians 4.
Ephesians 1.
</margin>
In the books of the New Testament, however, we are taught that the promised Christ (who is God over all, blessed forever) was foreshadowed and symbolized by the sacrifices of the Old Testament. He was finally sent by the Father at the time He had appointed—a time, I say, when iniquity was overflowing. He was sent and became incarnate, not because of anyone's good works (for all were sinners), but so that He might show the overflowing riches of His grace which He had promised, and save us according to His mercy.

In the New Testament, it is most clearly shown that Jesus Christ, the true lamb and the true sacrifice for the world, came to reconcile us with the Father. For He Himself is our peace, washing us from our sins in His own blood, liberating us from the slavery of the Devil (whom we served by sinning), so that we might be adopted as God's children through Him and be made His co-heirs.

<margin>
Acts 2, 10.
Titus 3.
Matthew 3, 28.
Romans 8.
Galatians 5.
1 Corinthians 12.
Ephesians 1, 3, 4.
</margin>
To ensure we recognize this singular and supreme benefit of God toward us, God gives us His Holy Spirit, whose fruit and gift is faith in God and His Christ. For without the Holy Spirit, by whom we are sealed, we can neither believe that God the Father sent the Messiah, nor that Jesus is the Christ. For as Paul says: "No one can say, 'Jesus is Lord,' except by the Holy Spirit." This same Spirit bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God, and pours into our hearts that charity <note>The Latin 'charitas' implies a selfless, divine love rather than just modern 'charity.'</note> which Paul describes to the Corinthians. Furthermore, He grants us Hope—the certain expectation of eternal life—of which He Himself is the guarantee and pledge. He also grants other spiritual gifts, which Paul mentions to the Galatians. Therefore, through this trust and faith in Christ, which works through love and expresses itself in acts of love, we are justified and sanctified. That is, God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ (who has also become our Father through Him, our brother) regards us as righteous and holy, by His grace not counting our sins against us unto hell.

Finally, Christ Himself came so that we, being sanctified and purified from sins through Him, might pursue His will through good works and renounce the things of the flesh. We are to serve Him freely in righteousness and holiness all our days, and show through good works (which God prepared so that we should walk in them) that we have been called to this grace. Indeed, anyone who does not have good works testifies that they do not have the kind of faith in Christ that He requires of us.

<margin>
Philippians 2.
2 Corinthians 5.
1 Timothy 2.
1 Peter 2.
1 John 2.
Hebrews 4, 7, 8, 9.
Matthew 11.
</margin>
We must approach Him and follow Him with a cheerful heart so that He may teach us. For He is our teacher, gentle and humble of heart; He is our example, from whom we must learn the rule of living rightly. Moreover, He is our Bishop and High Priest, the one mediator between God and men. He now sits at the right hand of God the Father, acting as our advocate, praying and interceding for us. Without a doubt, He will obtain for us whatever we ask of Him, or of the Father in His name—provided that, in asking, we believe He will do so. For this is what He promised. Therefore, let us not doubt, whenever we have sinned, to approach the throne of His grace with repentance (to which He invited and urged us at the very start of His preaching) and with confidence, believing that we have obtained mercy. For this is why He came: to save sinners by His grace.

<margin>
Acts 10.
Matthew 25.
</margin>
This Jesus Christ is to come again. After the "man of sin" <note>A reference to the Antichrist, often cited from 2 Thessalonians 2:3.</note> has been slain by the breath of His mouth, He will sit in His majesty to judge all people, rendering to each according to what they did in the body, whether good or evil. He will say to those on His right, who looked forward to future blessings in this world: "Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world." But to those on the left: "Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the Devil and his angels." Then indeed will be the end, when He delivers the kingdom to God the Father.

So that we might know these things, the Holy Bible has been handed down to us by the goodness of God through His Holy Spirit—so that we may know, I say, and believe that there is only one true God, and Jesus Christ whom He sent; and that believing, we may have life in His name.

No one can lay any other foundation than this one. Paul even wishes that anyone who announces any other faith or salvation than through Jesus Christ be accursed, even if it were an angel from heaven.

For from Him, and through Him, and in Him are all things: to Him, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be honor and glory forever and ever, Amen.

<meta>This page transitions from the general summary of the Bible to a detailed alphabetical index. It serves as a study guide, providing Greek and Hebrew etymologies for key theological terms and directing the reader to specific chapter and verse locations in the New Testament. This index helps the reader navigate the text through a scholarly, linguistic, and doctrinal lens.</meta>

# INDEX
## Of certain words, with the demonstration of specific passages pertaining to the understanding of the truth.

->The first number indicates the chapter, the latter the verse.<-

### A.

**ABBA**, a common Hebrew word in those times when the Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, lived on earth, derived from their true and native speech; it signifies that which is "Father" <note>Original Latin: Pater</note> to the Latins. *Mark 14:36, Romans 8:15, Galatians 4:6.*
**Abomination**, an accursed or detestable thing <note>Original Greek: βδέλυγμα</note>, which horribly offends the senses and the soul. *Matthew 24:15, Mark 13:14, Luke 21:20.*
**Absolution from sins**, a release or dismissal <note>Original Greek: αφεσις and λύσις</note>. *Matthew 16:19 and John 20:23.* To this is opposed "to bind" or "to tie" <note>Original Greek: δεῖσαι</note>, and "to retain" <note>Original Greek: κρατῆσαι</note>.
**Abstinence**, <note>Original Greek: ἐγκράτεια</note>, *2 Peter 1:6.* He abstains <note>Original Greek: ἐγκρατεύεται</note>, *1 Corinthians 9:25.* To abstain <note>Original Greek: ἀπέχεσθαι</note>, *1 Peter 2:11, 1 Thessalonians 4:3 and 5:22.*
**Abuse of Scripture** indicated and noted, *Matthew 4:6-7 and following, 2 Corinthians 2:17, Galatians 1:7, Ephesians 5:6, 2 Thessalonians 2:2, 2 Peter 3:3-4, 16, Jude verses 16 and following.* The perversity of the Antichrist in this kind as well, *2 Thessalonians 2:2.* Of the Pharisees, *Matthew 23:26.* Of others, *2 Timothy 2:16 and 3:7, Titus 1:10.* Of the Jews, *John 2:20.* To this same category are referred the deserters and corruptors of the truth of heavenly doctrine, and its enemies, *1 John 2:26, 2 Peter 2:1, Ephesians 4:14, 2 Thessalonians 2:2, 2 Timothy 3:7, Titus 1:10, Jude 1:4, 16, Revelation 18:3.*
**Acceptance of persons** <term>Partiality or favoritism based on outward appearance or status</term>, <note>Original Greek: προσωποληψία</note>; it is not found with God, *Acts 10:35, Romans 2:11, Galatians 2:6, Ephesians 6:9, Colossians 3:25, 1 Peter 1:17.* It is also forbidden to men, *James 2:1.*
**Accuser**, <note>Original Greek: κατήγορος</note>, *Acts 25:7.* The Devil as accuser, *Revelation 12:10.* To accuse and to be accused <note>Original Greek: κατηγορεῖν and κατηγορεῖσθαι</note>, *Matthew 12:2, Mark 3:22, Luke 6:2, Acts 19:38.* An accusing conscience, *Romans 2:15.* Christ accused, *Matthew 27:3, Mark 15:3 and following, Luke 23:2-3, John 18:30.* Paul accused, *Acts 22:30, 23:7, 25:5, 7, and 26:7,* where the word for "being summoned" <note>Original Greek: ἐγκαλεῖσθαι</note> is used.
**Adam**, the first man, *Luke 3:38, Romans 5:12, 14, 18, 1 Corinthians 15:2, 1 Timothy 2:13.* The second Adam, *Romans 5:14, 18, 1 Corinthians 15:45,* referring to Christ.
**Adoration of God**, worship <note>Original Greek: προσκύνησις</note>, *Matthew 4:10, John 4:20-21 and following.* Prayer <note>Original Greek: προσευχή</note>, *Acts 10:25, 14:11, 16:15, and 17:23,* where the word meaning "to revere" <note>Original Greek: σεβάζεσθαι or σέβεσθαι</note> is used, *Matthew 15:10.* Again, religious worship <note>Original Greek: θρησκεία</note>, *1 Corinthians 14:25, 1 Thessalonians 1:9.* The Apostle uses the word for "to serve" <note>Original Greek: δουλεύειν</note>, by which service is signified. Again, worship <note>Original Greek: προσκύνησis</note>, *Revelation 4:10, 14:7, 9, 11, 15:4, 19:4, and 22:8-9.* Adoration of the beast, *Revelation 13:4, 14:9, 16:2, and 19:10.* Superstitious adoration, *Acts 10:3, 9, and 14:11-12.*
**Advent of Christ**, his coming <note>Original Greek: παρουσία</note>, *Matthew 24:27, 1 Thessalonians 2:19, 3:13, 4:15, 5:2, James 5:7.* In *1 Timothy 6:14, 2 Timothy 4:8, and Titus 2:13,* it is called an "appearing" <note>Original Greek: ἐπιφάνεια</note>.
**Adultery** forbidden. This is <note>Original Greek: μοιχεία</note>, *Matthew 5:27-28, 14:4, 19:9, Mark 10:11-12, Luke 6:18, John 8:18, John 8:4, Romans 7:3, 13:9, Galatians 5:20, 1 Corinthians 6:13-14, Hebrews 13:4, James 4:4, 2 Peter 2:14.*
**Advocate**, comforter <note>Original Greek: παράκλητος</note>, regarding Christ, *1 John 2:1.* Regarding the Holy Spirit, *John 14:16.*
**Edification**, used metaphorically to mean growth and stability—a Hebrew phrase, *Romans 14:1, 15:1, 2 Corinthians 10:8, 12:19, 13:10, 1 Timothy 1:4.*
**Altar**, <note>Original Greek: θυσιαστήριον</note>, from the word "to sacrifice" <note>Original Greek: θύειν</note>, which are called sacrifices by the Latins, *1 Corinthians 9:13, Hebrews 13:26.*
**Friends**, <note>Original Greek: φίλοι</note>, *John 15:14-15.*
**Love toward God** or affection, and "to love," <note>Original Greek: ἀγάπη and ἀγαπᾷν</note>, *Matthew 22:37, Luke 10:27, John 14:21 and following, and 21:15-16, 1 Corinthians 8:3, Philippians 1:3, 1 John 2:5.* Self-love, *1 Corinthians 10:24, 33, and 13:5, Philippians 2:3, 2 Timothy 3:2,* where the "lovers of self" <note>Original Greek: φíλαυτοι</note> are named, *2 Peter 2:10.* If the scripture reading is correct which has "love-feasts" <note>Original Greek: ἀγάπας</note>, they signify the gatherings and banquets of Christians showing brotherly love. Love of glory, *John 12:43.* See also the entries for Charity and Lust.
**Angel**, <note>Original Greek: ἄγγελος</note>; the name, common in Latin speech, signifies a "Messenger" when translated. There are good and bad angels. Of the bad angels it is said, *Matthew 25:41,* where mention is made of the fire prepared for the Devil and his angels. But when angels are named in Scripture, they almost always indicate heavenly spirits serving to carry out the divine will. "Archangel" signifies a chief angel, just as <note>Original Greek: ἀρχάγγελος</note> refers to the master of a banquet, and <note>Original Greek: ἀρχιατρὸς</note> a chief physician. Mention of these is made in *Mark 12:25.* They served Christ, *Matthew 4:11, Mark 1, 2, Luke 22:43.* They are present for the faithful of Christ, *Matthew 18:11, 19, Hebrews 1:4-5 and following.* They appear, *Matthew 1:12, 2:13, Luke 1:26 and following, and 2:9 and following.* They are seen in human form, *Mark 16:5, Luke 24:4, John 20:12, Acts 1:10, 16:3.* They will come with Christ to judgment, *Matthew 25:31, Mark 8:38, Luke 9:26, 2 Thessalonians 1:7.*

<column-break/>

**Soul**, <note>Original Greek: ψυχή</note>. This name signifies life, as in *Matthew 2:20 and 6:25, Luke 12:19 and 14:26, John 10:11, 13:37, and 15:13, Acts 15:20 and 20:10.* It signifies in some places a condition or state, as some have interpreted *Acts 20:10* concerning the dead boy, though it seems more likely to say that life had already been restored. In some places it means the mind, that is, the affection of the heart, as in *Matthew 22:37 and 26:38, Mark 14:34.* And, as some have suspected, *John 12:25 and following,* although there life is clearly signified; *Luke 1:46 and 2:35, Acts 14:22 and 15:24.* In some places it means the spiritual and immortal nature in man, as in *Matthew 10:28, Mark 8:35-36, 2 Corinthians 1:23 and 12:15, Hebrews 10:38 and 13:17, Revelation 6:9 and 20:4.* In some places it means the understanding and the will of the mind together, as in *1 Thessalonians 5:14,* where they are named "faint-hearted" <note>Original Greek: ὀλιγόψυχοι</note>, endowed with a small soul, who do not yet have firm judgment, and whose opinion and will are more timid and unstable; *Hebrews 6:19, 2 Peter 2:14.* Although it can be understood that the man himself is signified in that place by the custom of Hebrew speech, as in *Acts 7:14, Romans 13:3.*
**Antichrist**, <note>Original Greek: Αντίχριστος</note>. This word, also common in Latin, signifies an adversary of Christ, or one setting himself against and opposite to Christ. In *Matthew 24:24* there are "false Christs" <note>Original Greek: ψευδόχριστοι</note>. Mention is made of this kind appearing even in the times of the Apostles, and of the kingdom of the Antichrist, in *2 Thessalonians 2:3, 1 John 2:13, 18, Mark 13:6.* Concerning the wicked deeds of the Antichrist, *2 Thessalonians 2:9, Revelation 19:20 and 20:10.*
That **Antiquity** is honorable is shown by the commandment regarding honoring the elders, *1 Timothy 5:1.* And what kind of elders these ought to be, *Titus 2:2.*
**Apostles**, <note>Original Greek: ἀπόστολοι</note>, a name also common in Latin usage, signifies an envoy, that is, one who is sent somewhere with instructions. But it is used in the Evangelical writings for ministers chosen in a special way by God for the proclamation <note>Original Greek: κήρυγμα</note> of the Gospel. Mention of these is made in *Luke 9:2, John 6:37 and following, and 15:16, Acts 1, 2, and 5:2.* Of Paul as the Apostle of the Gentiles, *Romans 1:5 and 15:16, 1 Corinthians 1:1, 9:1, 16 and following, Galatians 1:1 and 2:2, 1 Timothy 2:7, 2 Timothy 1:1.* Of their proper office, *1 Corinthians 12:28-29, Ephesians 4:11, 1 Corinthians 1:17.* Christ as the eminent and great Apostle, *Hebrews 3:1.* Of the twelve, *Matthew 10:3, 6, 7.* Of Peter as the Apostle of the Jews, *Galatians 2:8.* Epaphroditus the Apostle, *Philippians 2:25.* Of false apostles, who are <note>Original Greek: ψευδαπόστολοι</note>, *2 Corinthians 11:13.*
**Spiritual weapons**, *Romans 13:12, 2 Corinthians 6:7 and 10:4, Ephesians 6:11, 1 Thessalonians 5:8, 1 Peter 5:9.* These are "arms" <note>Original Greek: ὅπλα</note> with which the pious are fortified and defended.
**Arrogance**, see the entry for Pride.
**Ascension of Christ**. Concerning this, *Acts 1:9,* he was taken up <note>Original Greek: ἀνελήφθη</note>; *Luke 24:51,* he was carried into heaven <note>Original Greek: ἀνεφέρετο εἰς οὐρανὸν</note>; *Ephesians 4:9-10,* he who ascended <note>Original Greek: ἀναβὰς</note>; *1 Peter 3:22,* he who went into heaven <note>Original Greek: πορευθεὶς εἰς οὐρανὸν</note>; *Mark 16:9, 19 and 1 Timothy 3:16,* he was received up <note>Original Greek: ἀνελήφθη</note>. And the day of the ascension <note>Original Greek: ἡμέραι τῆς ἀναλήψεως</note>, *Luke 9:51.*
**Avarice**, <note>Original Greek: πλεονεξία</note>, *Luke 12:15,* by which name is signified greed and the desire to acquire more. And there are "lovers of money" <note>Original Greek: φιλάργυροι</note>, *Luke 16:14,* that is, those greedy for money, the name for which is silver; "love of money" <note>Original Greek: φιλαργυρία</note>, *1 Timothy 6:10.* Concerning this also *Matthew 26:9, John 12:15, Acts 5:6 and 24:3, 1 Corinthians 5:10-11 and 6:10, 2 Corinthians 9:6, Ephesians 5:3, Colossians 3:5, 1 Timothy 6:10, 2 Timothy 3:2, Hebrews 13:5, 2 Peter 2:3.*

### B.

**Babylon**, the proper name of a Chaldean city, signifies "confusion," *Revelation 14:8, 16:19, and 18:2.*
**Baptism** and **Baptizing**, <note>Original Greek: βαπτισμὸς and βάπτισμα</note>, signifies immersion or wetting, from the verb <note>Original Greek: βαπτίζω</note>, *Matthew 3:11 and 28:19, Mark 1:4 and 16:16, Luke 3:7, 16, John 1:25 and following, 3:3-5, and 4:1-2, Acts 2:38, 8:12, 9:18, 10:37, and 16:15, 19:3, 1 Corinthians 1:13 and following, Ephesians 5:26, 1 Peter 3:21.* Signifying washing and regeneration through Christ, *John 3:12, 16, Acts 2:38 and 12:16, Romans 6:3-4, 1 Peter 3:21, Ephesians 5:26.*

# INDEX OF WORDS AND PLACES

*Titus 3:5.* Nothing is profitable without faith, *Mark 16:16, 1 Corinthians 10:2, 1 Peter 3:21.* **Baptism** is one, *Ephesians 4:5.* Its ministry is human, *Matthew 3:11, John 1:31 & 3:5 & 4:1-2, Acts 8:12 & following, & 9:18 & 22:16.* The efficacy belongs to Christ, *Matthew 3:11, Mark 1:4, Luke 3:7, 16, John 1:33.* It signifies the visible gifts of the Holy Spirit, *Acts 1:5 & 11:16 & 19:5.* It also signifies affliction or suffering, *Mark 10:13, Luke 18:15.*

**Baptist** <note>original: Baptista</note> is **The Baptist** <note>original Greek: Βαπτιστής</note>, a name derived from the same verb from which "baptism" comes; and by this common name, **washing** <note>original Greek: βαπτισμός</note> signifies specifically John the son of Zechariah, who was divinely sent to baptize before Christ, *Matthew 3:1 & 11:11-12 & 14:2, Mark 6:14 & 8:28, Luke 7:20 & 9:7-8.*

**Blessed**, **the happy ones** <note>original Greek: μακάριοι</note>, *Matthew 5:3 & 11:6 & 13:10 & 16:17 & 24:46, Luke 1:45 & 6:20-21 & 10:23 & 11:27 & 12:37 & 14:14, John 13:17, 1 Peter 3:14 & 4:14, James 1:12, Revelation 1:3 & 14:13 & 16:15 & 19:9 & 22:14.*

**Blessedness**, this is the glory of Christians, that is **life** <note>original Greek: ζωή</note>, and eternal life with Christ, and the **Kingdom of Heaven** <note>original Greek: βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν</note>.

**Beelzebub**, or as the Greeks say, **Beelzebul** <note>original Greek: Βεελζεβούλ</note>, a Hebrew name which carries the meaning of "Lord of Flies," and this name is attributed to the prince of devils, *Matthew 10:15 & 12:27, Mark 3:22, Luke 11:15.*

**Blessing and to bless**, **eulogy** <note>original Greek: εὐλογία</note> and **to speak well of** <note>original Greek: εὐλογεῖν</note>. In the sense of praising and praying for good, *Matthew 5:44, Luke 1:28, 42 & 2:28 & 24:53, Romans 1:25 & 9:5 & 12:14, 1 Corinthians 14:16, James 3:9.* Used for prosperity and happiness, *Matthew 15:36, Mark 10:16, Luke 24:50 & following, Acts 3:25, Galatians 3:8, Ephesians 1:3, 1 Peter 2:9.* Used for generosity and alms-giving, *2 Corinthians 9:5-6.* Used for the giving of thanks and the celebration of the sacred rite <note>Referring to the Eucharist</note>, *1 Corinthians 10:16-17.* But the use of this word is entirely unique and its particular reality must be investigated according to the logic of the Hebrew language.

**To do good**, **to act rightly** <note>original Greek: καλῶς ποιεῖν</note>. Good must be done to enemies, *Matthew 5:44, Romans 12:17, 20.* Good must be done to all, *John 3:20, Romans 12:20, Galatians 6:9-10, James 2:8.* Especially to those joined in faith, *Galatians 6:10.*

**To blaspheme**, **to speak evil** <note>original Greek: βλασφημεῖν</note>, and **blasphemous**, **evil-speaker** <note>original Greek: βλάσφημος</note>; these are Greek words changed into the form of Latin speech. It signifies a curse of atrocious injury, specifically against God, or divine things, or among divine works; to which is opposed **good report** <note>original Greek: εὐφημία</note> and **fame** <note>original Greek: διαφημία</note>, *Matthew 12:31, Mark 3:28, Luke 12:10, 1 Timothy 1:13, Romans 2:24.*

## C.

**Chalice and cup**, *Matthew 26:28, Mark 14:22, Luke 22:19.* By common name indicating a certain shape of a drinking vessel. In Hebrew custom, it also signifies the portion of miseries and sad sorrows that each must drain, just as the Latins used the word "to swallow."

**Head**, **the top** <note>original Greek: κεφαλή</note>. The head of Christ is God, *1 Corinthians 11:3.* Christ is the head of the Church, *Ephesians 1:10, 22 & 4:15 & 5:23, Colossians 1:18 & 2:10, 19.* Christ is the head of man, *1 Corinthians 11:3.* The head of all principality, *Colossians 2:10.*

**Charity**, **love** <note>original Greek: ἀγάπη</note>. God is love, *1 John 4:8.* The love of God toward us, *John 3:16 & 13:34 & 15:27, Romans 5:8 & 8:35, Ephesians 1:5-6 & 2:4 & 5:2, 2 Timothy 1:9, 1 John 2:5 & 3:1.* Love toward others, *John 15:17, Romans 12:9 & 10, 1 Corinthians 16:14, 2 Corinthians 2:4, Ephesians 4:15 & 5:2, Philippians 2:1, Colossians 3:14, Hebrews 10:24 & 13:1, 1 Peter 4:8, 2 Peter 1:7, 1 John 4:12.* The same toward enemies, *Matthew 5:44, Luke 6:27 & 33, Acts 7:60, Romans 12:20, 1 Peter 3:9.* This is the sign indicating Christ's faithful, *John 13:35.* The fruit of the Spirit of God, *Galatians 5:22.* The bond of perfection, *Colossians 3:14.* The fulfillment of the Law, *Matthew 7:12, Romans 13:10, Galatians 5:14, 1 Timothy 1:5.* The outworking of this, *Romans 12:10, 1 Corinthians 8:2 & 13:4 & following, 1 Peter 4:9.* It grows cold in the last times, *Matthew 24:12.*

**Flesh**, **meat** <note>original Greek: σάρξ</note>. Sometimes it signifies only "man" according to the custom of the Hebrew language, *Luke 3:6, Acts 2:17, 1 Peter 1:24.* Human life and nature, *Hebrews 5:7, Romans 9:8, 1 Peter 4:2.* The senses, *Matthew 26:41, John 6:63.* Sometimes, as is most common in the Pauline Epistles, it signifies the vicious and corrupt nature passed down after the fall of our first parents to all posterity, and thoughts that are depraved and inconsistent with divine things, *Matthew 16:12, 1 Corinthians 15:39, John 3:36 & 6:63, Romans 8:5 & Romans 7:14,* where he is also called **carnal** <note>original Greek: σαρκικός</note>, *and 1 Corinthians 3:1-2 & following, 2 Peter 2:10.* Works of the flesh <note>original Greek: ἔργα τῆς σαρκός</note>, *Galatians 4:23 & 5:16-17, Ephesians 2:3.* The flesh of Christ, the bread of God, and the heavenly bread <note>original Greek: ἄρτος ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ and ἄρτος τοῦ Θεοῦ</note>, *John 6:50.*

**Chastisement**, **discipline** <note>original Greek: παιδεία</note>, and **to chastise** <note>original Greek: παιδεύειν</note>, *Hebrews 12:5-6, 1 Corinthians 11:32, Ephesians 6:4, Revelation 3:19.*

**Chastity**, **purity** <note>original Greek: ἁγνεία</note>, *1 Timothy 5:2, Titus 2:12, 2 Corinthians 6:6, Hebrews 13:4, 1 Peter 3:2.*

**Christians** first called so at Antioch, **Acts** 11:26.

**Christ**, **the Anointed** <note>original Greek: Χριστός</note>, who is the Messiah, and has the meaning of "Anointed One" and "King": the proper title of Jesus our Lord and Savior. Christ is God, the beginning and the end, *Matthew 1, 1:16, John 1:24 & 10:31 & 20:21, Acts 20:21, Romans 9:5 & 14:18.*

# INDEX OF WORDS AND PLACES.

*1 Peter 2:24; 1 John 3:5; Matthew 26:28; 1 John 1:7; Hebrews 9:14; Revelation 1:5 & 5:9 & 7:14.* Our merit, *1 Corinthians 1:30; 2 Corinthians 5:19.* Propitiation, Reconciliation, Redemption, Satisfaction for sins, *Romans 3:25 & 5:11; 2 Corinthians 5:19; Ephesians 1:7; Colossians 1:20; 1 Timothy 2:6; 1 John 2:2; 1 Peter 1:18-19; Galatians 2:20; Revelation 5:9.* Forgiveness and remedy through him, *Acts 4:2, 13 & 10:43; 2 Corinthians 5:18-19.* Sitting in heaven at the right hand of the Father, *Mark 16:19; Luke 24:51; Acts 1:9 & 2:34 & 3:21 & 7:49; Romans 3:34; Ephesians 1:20; Colossians 3:1; Hebrews 1:13 & 9:24 & 10:13; 1 Peter 3:22.* Departed and yet present, *Matthew 26:24, 28; Mark 14:21, 23; John 12:8, 29 & 16:14; 2 Corinthians 5:5, 17; Matthew 18:20 & 28:20; Ephesians 3:17; 2 Corinthians 13:5.* Having all things subject to himself, *Matthew 11:3, 27 & 28:18; Luke 10:22; John 3:35 & 13:3 & 16:15 & 17:10; Romans 14:8; 1 Corinthians 15:28; Ephesians 1:22; Philippians 2:9 & following; Colossians 1:15 & following; Hebrews 2:8; 1 Peter 3:22; Revelation 1:5, 18.* Head of the Church, *Ephesians 1:12 & 4:15 & 5:23; Colossians 1:18 & 2:19.* Filling all in all, *Colossians 1:17.* Judge of the living and the dead, *Acts 10:42 & 17:31; Matthew 25:31 & following; John 5:27; Romans 14:11; 1 Corinthians 4:5; 2 Corinthians 5:10; 2 Timothy 4:1.* Adoration and invocation of him, *Matthew 2:3, 11 & 28:9, 17; Mark 1:40; Luke 5:12 & 17:16 & 24:52; John 9:39; Philippians 2:10; Hebrews 1:6; Matthew 8:1 & 20:30 & 25:11; Mark 10:47; Luke 18:13; 2 Timothy 2:22.* His manifest coming, sudden as lightning, *Matthew 24:3, 27, 37; Mark 13:26, 33, 35; Luke 17:24 & 21:27, 35; Acts 1:12 & 3:20; 1 Thessalonians 5:2; 2 Thessalonians 1:7-8; 2 Peter 3:4, 10; Revelation 16:14-15.* An example for us, *John 12:25 & 13:15, 34; 1 Corinthians 4:17 & 11:1; Ephesians 5:2; Philippians 2:5 & 3:10; Hebrews 13:8, 13; 1 Peter 2:21.* To be confessed before men, *Matthew 10:32; Mark 8:38; Luke 9:26 & 12:8; John 12:25, 48; Romans 10:10; 2 Corinthians 4:13; 2 Timothy 2:13; Hebrews 10:23; 1 John 2:22 & following.*

**Circumcision**, <note>original Greek: περιτομή</note>, properly signifies a "cutting around," which was commanded by God to be used as a mystical sign among the Jewish people, and <note>original Greek: καὶ ὑπαλλαγὴν</note> <note>by exchange/substitution</note> for the Jewish people themselves. Just as the "foreskin" signifies the other nations. Circumcision of the flesh, *Romans 2:25 & following; 1 Corinthians 7:18-19.*

**Keys of the heavens**, signify the power in the Church of absolving sinners or not absolving them, by which the kingdom of heaven is thus opened or closed, *Matthew 16:19; John 20:23; Matthew 18:18.* Key of knowledge, *Luke 11:52.* Of death and hell, *Revelation 1:18.*

**Heaven will pass away**, *Matthew 24:35; Luke 21:33; 2 Peter 3:10; Revelation 21:1.* Opened, *Matthew 3:17; Acts 7:56.* New, *2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:1.*

**Lord’s Supper**, <note>original Greek: δεῖπνον κυριακόν</note>, *1 Corinthians 11:20.* <note>original Greek: τράπεζα Κυρίου</note>, that is, the table of the Lord, *1 Corinthians 10:21.* And in the same place, its true use. Institution, *Matthew 26:26 & following; Mark 24:12; Luke 22:19.* Frequent use, *Acts 2:46 & 20:7.*

**Knowledge** of oneself through the law, *Romans 2:7 & 3:20 & 7:7-8.* Of God by all, so that they are without excuse, *Romans 1:20.* Of salvation, *John 17:3; Galatians 4:9; 2 Peter 1:2 & 3:17; 1 John 2:3, 5, 22.* Full knowledge through Christ, *Matthew 11:27; John 17:3; 1 Corinthians 1:3, 9-10; 1 John 3:2, 24.* Which the world does not have, *John 1:10 & 5:38 & following, & 9:39 & 17:9; 1 Corinthians 1:21; John 3:19-20.*

**Collection**, which is also an offering, <note>original Greek: λογία</note>, *1 Corinthians 16:1-2; 2 Corinthians 8:2 & following, & 9:1 & following; Acts 11:29; Romans 15:26.*

**Colony**, *Acts 16:12.* A Latin name; in Greek it is <note>original Greek: ἀποικία</note>, one city led out from another.

**Common**, in the custom of the Hebrew language, means unclean and polluted, *Acts 10:14 & following; Mark 7:15-16 & following; Romans 14:14; Titus 1:16.*

**Concord** and those who are of one mind and in agreement, feeling the same thing, *Acts 5:12; Romans 15:6-7; Philippians 1:27; 1 Peter 3:8.*

**Concupiscence**, an appetite and craving of a depraved mind, *Matthew 5:28; Mark 4:19; Romans 6:12 & 7:7-8 & 13:9; Galatians 5:16-17, 24; James 1:1 & 4:1, 3; 2 Peter 1:4 & 2:10 & 3:3; 1 John 2:16.*

**Confession**, *Matthew 10:32; Luke 12:8; John 1:20 & following; Hebrews 13:15.* It also signifies preaching and the giving of thanks, *Matthew 11:25; Luke 2:38 & 10:21; Romans 15:9.* Confession of sins, *Mark 1:5; Luke 15:18-19 & following, & 18:13; 1 John 1:9.* Public confession, *Matthew 3:6; Mark 1:5; Acts 2:38 & 19:3.* Confession of offenses for reconciliation, *James 5:16.* To which also belongs the doctrine, *Matthew 5:24; Luke 12:58.*

**Confidence** or trust, <note>original Greek: πεποίθησις</note>, *2 Corinthians 1:9 & 2:4 & 7:4; Ephesians 3:12; Philippians 1:25.* See the word **Faith**.

**Good conscience**, *Hebrews 13:18.* Toward God and men, *Acts 23:1 & 24:16; 2 Corinthians 1:12; 1 Timothy 1:19 & 3:9; 2 Timothy 1:3; Hebrews 9:14 & 10:2; 1 Peter 3:16.* Bad conscience, *1 Timothy 4:2.*

**Counsel**, <note>original Greek: γνώμη</note>, *1 Corinthians 2:16.* <note>original Greek: συνέδριον</note>, which was a council, *Acts 5:21, 27.* To deliberate, <note>original Greek: συμβουλεύεσθαι</note>, *Matthew 26:4.* <note>original Greek: βούλημα</note>, *Acts 5:34.* An example of good counsel, *John 7:24, 51; Acts 5:35 & following; Matthew 12:29 & 22:21, 27 & 26:52 & 27:19 & 28:7; John 1:50; Acts 4:19.*

**Divine consolation**, *Romans 15:4-5; 2 Corinthians 1:3 & 7:4, 6; Philippians 2:17-18; 2 Thessalonians 2:16.* Through the scriptures, *Romans 15:4.* Brotherly consolation, *Acts 15:3, 31 & 20:32.* Which is <note>original Greek: παράκλησις</note> and <note>original Greek: παραμυθία</note>, *Acts 15:32; Romans 15:14; 2 Corinthians 2:8; 1 Thessalonians 5:12, 14; Philippians 2:1.* To <note>original Greek: παρακαλέω</note> means both to entreat and to console, *Acts 25:32.*

<column-break/>

**Constancy** or perseverance, <note>original Greek: ὑπομονή</note>, *Acts 14:20; 2 Peter 1:30; James 5:7 & following.* <note>original Greek: ὑπομονή</note>, patience, the doctrine and examples of this, *Matthew 10:22, 38 & 24:13; 2 Timothy 3:10; Ephesians 4:2 & 6:20; 1 Thessalonians 2:4; 2 Timothy 4:2; Hebrews 4:14; Revelation 2:2, 10.*

**To be content**, that is, to require nothing further, *Luke 3:14; 1 Corinthians 7:31-32; Philippians 4:6, 11; 1 Timothy 6:6; Hebrews 13:5.*

**Conversion** of Peter, *Luke 22:62.* Of Paul, *Acts 9:6 & following.*

**Horn**, in the Hebrew custom, means power and strength, *Luke 1:69.* <note>The text lists 1:96, likely a typo for 1:69.</note>

**Body**, mortal and subject to sins, *Romans 6:12 & 7:24 & 8:10 & following; 1 Corinthians 15:44, 50.* It is called a dwelling and a tabernacle, *2 Corinthians 5:1; 2 Peter 1:13-14.* It must be mortified <note>put to death</note>, *Romans 8:13; 2 Corinthians 4:10 & following; Colossians 3:5.* An earthen vessel, *2 Corinthians 4:7.* Temple of the Holy Spirit, *1 Corinthians 6:19.* It will rise again as a spiritual body, *Romans 6:4 & following; 1 Corinthians 15:44; 2 Corinthians 4:16.* The assembly of believers, *Ephesians 3:10 & following; Colossians 1:18, 24 & 4:1, 15.* It signifies the reality itself, *Colossians 2:19.* The body of Christ as a temple, *John 2:21; Matthew 27:40.* The bread is the Body of Christ, *Matthew 26:27; Mark 14:22; Luke 22:19.*

**Reproof**, see **Chastisement**.

**Creature**, subject to vanity, *Romans 8:20.* A new creature, *2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15.*

**To believe**, Abraham believed God, *Romans 4:3; Galatians 3:6.* It happens just as the Centurion believed, *Matthew 8:13.* Believe the Gospel, *Mark 1:15.* The Gospel is the power of God to everyone who believes, *Romans 1:16.* He who believes in the Son does not perish, *John 3:15 & following.* Those ordained to life believe, *Acts 13:48.* Those believing in Christ have remission of sins and are children of God, *Acts 10:43 & 13:38; Galatians 2:16; John 1:12; Romans 8:14-15 & following.*

**Cross**, torture or passion; the cross of Christ and the preaching of the cross, *1 Corinthians 1:18, 23.* Each must bear his own cross, *Matthew 10:38 & 16:24; Mark 8:34; Luke 9:23 & 14:27; John 12:15; Acts 14:22; Romans 8:17, 29; 1 Corinthians 1:18, 23 & 4:9 & following; 2 Corinthians 11:23-24 & following; Philippians 1:17, 27, 30 & 3:10, 18; 2 Timothy 2:3, 9 & 3:12; 1 Peter 1:6 & 2:21 & 3:14 & 4:12-13.*

**Curiosity**, *2 Thessalonians 2:1; 1 Timothy 5:13.*

### D.

**Damnation**, *Romans 3:8 & 8:1; Revelation 15:1.*

**To give** or bestow, *Luke 6:37-38; Acts 20:35.*

See the word **Alms**.

**Tithe**, *Hebrews 7:5-7; Matthew 23:23.*

**Delights** <note>luxuries</note>, *Luke 7:25; 7:37 & 16:19 & following; 1 Timothy 5:6; 2 Peter 2:13; Revelation 18:3, 14.*

**Denarius**, and the denarium, a coin and currency, *Mark 6:37 & 12:16, 42 & 14:5; Acts 19:19; Revelation 6:6.* The Greek name is <note>original Greek: δηνάριος</note>, worth ten "asses" <note>a small Roman copper coin</note>. The drachma is doubled, <note>original Greek: δίδραχμον</note>, *Matthew 17:24 & following.*

**Census description**, by which the number of individuals is determined, *Luke 2:1-2.*

**Desolation**, *Matthew 24:15; Mark 13:14; Luke 21:20; Revelation 6:1.*

**God**, <note>original Greek: οὐσία</note>, which they call substance and essence; eternal, omnipotent, creator and governor of all things that have been founded. One, *Mark 12:29, 32; 1 Corinthians 8:6; Galatians 3:20; Ephesians 4:6; 1 Timothy 2:5.* Spirit, *John 4:24 & 5:20.* Known through the Holy Spirit, *John 4:16 & 15:26 & 16:13; Romans 8:16; 1 Corinthians 2:10 & following; 1 John 2:13, 27.* Invisible, *John 1:18 & 6:46; 1 Timothy 1:17; 1 John 4:20.* Alone good, *Matthew 19:17; Mark 10:18; Luke 18:19.* Alone wise, *Romans 16:27; 1 Timothy 1:17; Jude 1:25.* Alone holy, *Revelation 15:4.* Sole sovereign and having immortality, *1 Timothy 6:16.* Alone forgiving sins, *Mark 2:9-10; Luke 5:23-24.* Knowing his own, *2 Timothy 2:19.* Knowing hearts, *Acts 15:8; Romans 8:27; 1 Thessalonians 2:4; 1 John 3:20.* Justifying, sanctifying, and giving life, *John 17:17; Acts 17:28; Romans 3:29 & 4:5 & 8:33; Colossians 1:12, 14, 22; 1 Thessalonians 5:9; 1 Timothy 6:13.* Savior, *Titus 1:4 & 2:10, 13 & 3:6; Jude 1:25.* Alone to be adored, *Matthew 4:10; Luke 4:8; Revelation 19:10 & 22:8-9.* To be adored in spirit and truth, *John 4:24.* Does not dwell in temples made with hands, *Acts 7:48 & 17:24.* Having no counselors, *Romans 11:34; 1 Corinthians 2:16.* Omnipotent, *Matthew 19:26; Mark 10:27; Luke 1:37 & 18:27.* From whom, through whom, in whom are all things, *Romans 11:36; 1 Corinthians 8:6 & 15:28; Ephesians 1:23 & 4:6.* Working and effecting all things, *John 5:21-23; Romans 11:36; 1 Corinthians 12:6; 2 Corinthians 3:5-6; Ephesians 1:11; Philippians 1:6 & 2:13; Hebrews 13:21; Revelation 17:4.* Beginning and perfecting good works in us, *Philippians 1:6; Ephesians 3:20; 2 Corinthians 3:5-6.* From whence all good things come, *John 3:16; 1 Corinthians 4:7 & 6:11-12 & 12:5-6; 2 Corinthians 3:5 & 4:7; Ephesians 4:6-7; 1 Timothy 6:17; James 1:17; 2 Peter 1:3.* The gifts and calling of God are without regret <note>irrevocable</note>, *Romans 11:11.* Through him we live and move, *Acts 17:28.* He cares for us, *1 Peter 5:7.* Testing his own, *Hebrews 12:6-7; 1 Corinthians 11:2; James 1:12-13 & 5:7; 1 Peter 1:7 & 4:12; Revelation 2:10.* True and faithful, *John 3:33 & 8:14, 26; Romans 3:4; 1 Corinthians 1:18.*

# INDEX OF WORDS AND PLACES.

*1 Thessalonians 5:24; 2 Thessalonians 3:3; 2 Timothy 2:13; Titus 1:2; Hebrews 6:18 & 10:23; 1 John 1:9 & 5:6, 20.* Inviting to repentance, *Romans 2:4; 2 Peter 3:9.* Near to those who call upon Him, *Matthew 7:7, 8, 9 & 18:19, 20 & 21:22; Mark 11:24; Luke 11:9; John 16:23, 24 <note>The original text mistakenly cites Job 16, but the context and verses 23-24 point to the Gospel of John.</note>; Acts 2:21; Romans 10:8; 1 John 5:15.* To be imitated, *Ephesians 5:1; 1 John 2:6 & 4:11, 17, 19.* Head of Christ, *1 Corinthians 11:3.* Judge of all, *Hebrews 12:23; James 4:12.* Giver of the water of life, *Revelation 21:6.* The beginning and the end, *Revelation 21:6.* Dwelling in those who are faithful, *John 14:23; 2 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 2:6; 1 John 3:24.* Father of Spirits, *Hebrews 12:9.* A consuming fire, *Hebrews 12:29.* Father of all, *Ephesians 3:15.* Creator of all, *Ephesians 3:9; 1 Corinthians 11:12; Hebrews 3:3, 6; Revelation 4:11 & 10:6.*

**Devil**, a Greek name <note>original: "Diabolus"</note>, signifies a slanderer and the author of enmities and discords. **Tempter**, *Matthew 4:3; Mark 1:13, 14; Luke 4:1, 2; John 13:2; 1 Corinthians 7:5; 2 Thessalonians 3:5.* **Murderer** from the beginning, *John 8:44.* **Sinning** from the beginning, *1 John 3:8.* **Liar** and the father of lies, *John 8:44.* **Seducer** of the world, *Revelation 12:9 & 20:10.* **His sons** are the impious, *Matthew 13:39; John 8:44; 1 John 3:8, 10.* **Prince** of the world, *Matthew 4:9; Luke 4:5 and following; John 12:31 & 14:30 & 16:11.* **Dragon** and ancient serpent, *Revelation 12:3 and following.* Evil and malignant, *Matthew 6:13; 1 John 2:13, 14, 15.* **Angel**, *Matthew 25:41; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude verse 6; Revelation 12:7.* Powers and principalities, *Ephesians 6:12.* Prince of the power of this air, *Ephesians 2:2.* Accuser of the faithful, an evil **Spirit** <note>see the entry for **Spirit**</note>. Our adversary, *1 Peter 5:8.* Enemy, *Matthew 13:25, 28; Luke 10:30.* He who transforms himself into an **Angel of light**, *2 Corinthians 11:14.* For whom, along with his angels, perpetual fire is prepared, *Matthew 25:41; 2 Peter 2:17.*

**Day**, the significance of this is time, the distinction of which does not carry a religious necessity to observe, *Romans 14:5; Galatians 4:10; Colossians 2:16.*

**End days** and the final time now that Christ has come, *1 Corinthians 11:34; 1 Timothy 4:1; 2 Peter 3:3; 1 John 2:18, 28.*

**Finger of God**, is the power of God, using a Hebrew phrase, *Luke 11:20.* <note>The "Finger of God" is a biblical metaphor for divine intervention or power, notably used regarding the writing of the Ten Commandments and the casting out of demons.</note>

**Gods**, that is, princes and judges, *John 10:34, 35.* **Idols**, *Acts 14:19 & 17:23 & 19:26; 1 Corinthians 8:5 & 10:20; Galatians 4:8.*

**Disciples** of Christ, of what sort they are, *Matthew 10:16, 24, 38; John 8:31 & 14:15, 16 and following; Acts 1:13 and following.*

To discuss or reason from the Scriptures, *Acts 17:4.*

**The Rich**, it is difficult for them to receive the word of God, *Matthew 19:23.* And yet some are found who do so, *Matthew 27:57; Luke 19:2, 3.* Cursed are the rich who abuse their riches, *Luke 6:24 & 16:22; James 5:1, 2.* **The wickedness of the rich**, *James 2:6, 7.* **The Rich** made so by the beast, *Revelation 18:15, 19.*

**Riches.** Although these are a gift of God, *1 Timothy 6:17;* nevertheless, because they give occasion for many evils, they are called by the name of iniquity <note>original: "iniquitatis habent appellationem," referring to the "mammon of unrighteousness"</note>, *Luke 16:9.* No one can serve these and God at the same time, *Matthew 6:24, 25.* These are not to be lusted after, *1 Timothy 6:17, 18.* One must not trust in them, *Luke 11:15 and following; 1 Timothy 6:17.* And in the same place, minds should not be puffed up because of them, *James 1:10, 11.* In some people, these choke the word of God, *Matthew 13:22; Luke 8:14.* The end of the beast’s riches, *Revelation 18:11, 16.*

**Teachers** in the Church, *1 Corinthians 12:28; Ephesians 4:11; 1 Timothy 1:7; Acts 13:46 & 48.* Paul, teacher of the Gentiles, *1 Timothy 2:7.* Christ among the teachers, *Luke 2:46.*

**Doctrine**, true, *Matthew 7:20; John 7:16, 17; Acts 2:16; Romans 15:18; 1 Timothy 1:19, 20 & 4:13 & 5:6 & 6:17; 2 Timothy 3:3; Titus 1:16, 17; 2 John 9.* **New life**, *Mark 1:10; Acts 17:19.* **False doctrine**, *Matthew 15:8 & 16:2, 3; Mark 7:6 & 8:15; Ephesians 4:17, 18; Colossians 2:8; 1 Timothy 1:4 & 4:1, 2; 2 Timothy 4:4; Titus 1:10 & 2:8; Hebrews 13:9; 2 John 7, 10; Revelation 2:20.*

**Deceit**, a Greek name common in Latin speech <note>original: "Dolus"</note>, meaning fraud and snares, *Matthew 26:4; Mark 14:1.* <term>πανεργία</term> <gloss>guile or craftiness</gloss> and malice, *Acts 13:10.* The name "Deceit" signifies the same thing, *Luke 20:33; John 1:47; Romans 1:29; 2 Corinthians 12:16.* Perversity, *1 Peter 2:1.*

**Dominion**, *2 Peter 2:10; Jude 1:8; Colossians 1:16; Ephesians 1:21.*

**Lord**, <term>δεσπότης</term> <gloss>master or sovereign</gloss>, *2 Peter 2:18.* And <term>κύριος</term> <gloss>lord</gloss>, signifies him who possesses the primacy of power and governance. How lords <note>masters</note> ought to behave toward servants, *Ephesians 6:5; Colossians 4:1; 1 Timothy 6:1.* And interpreting the name <term>κύριος</term> <gloss>Lord</gloss>, they attributed it properly to the eternal God, translating the name Jehovah, *Matthew 22:37; Luke 20:37, 42.*

**Gifts of God**, *James 1:16; 1 Corinthians 7:17; Ephesians 2:8.* Without repentance, *Romans 11:29.* Diverse and peculiar, *Romans 12:6 and following; 1 Corinthians 7:17 & 12:4 and following; Ephesians 4:7, 11.*

**To Sleep**, is transferred to the end of life, and "those who sleep" are the dead, which is a phrase from the Hebrew language. It is understood as the departure of the soul, which is the destruction of the body now deprived of all movement and agitation, *1 Corinthians 15:16; 1 Thessalonians 4:13.*

<column-break/>

### E.

**Drunkenness** and **the drunk**, *Matthew 24:38; 1 Corinthians 11:21; Luke 21:34; Romans 13:13; Galatians 5:21; Ephesians 5:18.* Drunkards will not be heirs of the kingdom of God, *1 Corinthians 6:10.* One should not associate with them, *1 Corinthians 5:11.*

**Church**, a Greek name <note>original: "Ecclesia"</note>, has the meaning of a congregation and assembly. In the Evangelical and Apostolic writings, it properly denotes the community and gathering of those who believe the Gospel and are faithful, just as the <term>συναγωγή</term> <gloss>synagogue</gloss> of the Jews indicates. It is used for the holy and pious, *1 Corinthians 12:28; Ephesians 1:23 & 3:10, 21 & 5:23 and following; Colossians 1:18, 24.* **One**, *John 10:16 & 17:10, 21; Galatians 3:28.* **One body of Christ**, *Ephesians 1:2, 3 & 4:4, 12, 16; Colossians 1:19; Romans 12:4, 5; 1 Corinthians 10:17 & 12:12.* Its members are the faithful and the saints, *Romans 12:5; 1 Corinthians 12:12, 13.* **House of God**, *1 Timothy 3:15; Hebrews 3:6.* **Pillar and foundation of truth**, *1 Timothy 3:15.* **The fullness**, *Ephesians 1:23.* **Heavenly and new Jerusalem**, *Galatians 4:26; Revelation 3:12 & 21:2.* **Mother of the faithful**, *Galatians 4:26.* **City of God**, *Revelation 3:12.* In which God is the temple, *Revelation 21:22.* **Holy**, *Ephesians 5:27; 1 Corinthians 1:30; 2 Corinthians 1:1.* Used for the faithful of one place, *Acts 14:1, 43; Romans 16:4, 1; 1 Corinthians 1:2 & 16:1, 19; 2 Corinthians 1:1; Galatians 1:2; Colossians 4:1; 2 Thessalonians 1:1, 13; 1 Peter 5:1; Revelation 2:8, 13, 18.* Used for the faithful of one house, *Romans 16:5; 1 Corinthians 16:19; Colossians 4:15; Philippians 1:1.* **Women** in the Church should not teach, *1 Corinthians 14:34; 1 Timothy 2:12.* Women as ministers in the Church, *Romans 16:3; 1 Timothy 2:9.* Order must be maintained in the Church, *1 Corinthians 14:26, 40.* The Church must be heard, *Matthew 18:17.* It hears the voice of Christ alone, *John 8:47 & 10:3, 6 & 18:37; 2 John 9.* The Church is not contentious, *1 Corinthians 11:16.* The sole foundation of the Church is Christ, *Matthew 16:18; 1 Corinthians 3:11; Ephesians 2:20, 21.*

**The Elect** are the pious and holy who believe the Gospel, who are chosen out of the multitude of this world for salvation and eternal life, *Matthew 20:16 & 22:14 & 24:22; Mark 13:20; Romans 8:28, 29; 2 Timothy 2:10; Hebrews 12:5, 6; Colossians 3:12; 1 Peter 1:1.* These are the weak and despised in the world, *1 Corinthians 1, 27; James 2:5.* No accusation weighs against them, *Romans 8:1, 29.*

**Alms**, a Greek name <note>original: "Eleemosyna"</note>, signifies the affection and work of mercy in helping the needs of another, *Matthew 6:1 and following; Luke 11:41 & 12:33 & 14:13 & 16:9; Acts 10:31 & 24:17; Philippians 4:14; 1 John 3:17.*

**Bishop**, a Greek name <note>original: "Episcopus"</note>, signifies an inspector and overseer, presiding in the Church in the Apostolic writings, who is also an **Elder** and **Pastor**, *Philippians 1:1; 1 Timothy 3:1, 2; Titus 1:7.*

**Gospel**, a Greek name <note>original: "Evangelium"</note>, has the meaning of good news. It specifically denotes the herald of the kingdom of God, which is the preaching of divine grace and mercy promised in Christ and declared to the world at his coming. **Power**, that is, the potency of God, *Romans 1:16; 1 Corinthians 1:18.* The wisdom of God, *1 Corinthians 2:7.* The secret of the divine will, *Romans 16:25; Ephesians 1:9; Colossians 1:26.* **Revealing** the justice of God, *Romans 1:17.* The ministry of the spirit, *2 Corinthians 3:9.* Through which salvation is given, *1 Corinthians 15:1, 2; Ephesians 1:14.* **To be announced publicly**, *Matthew 10:27.* To every creature and in all the world, *Matthew 24:14 & 28:9; Mark 16:15; Acts 1:8.* A message contrary to this should not be heard even from a heavenly Angel, *Galatians 1:8.* Causes of division, *Matthew 10:34 and following; Mark 13:8 and following; Luke 12:51; Acts 13:5 & 16:20, 21 & 17:5, 13 & 18:12 & 19:23 & 21:13, 30; 2 Corinthians 6:3, 4 and following.* It is rejected by those who consider themselves wise and righteous, and is accepted by the simple and sinners, *Matthew 11:25 & 21:16; Luke 7:22; John 7:37 & 9:36; 1 Corinthians 1:18.* Obstacles to this assent, *Matthew 13:3 and following; John 5:38, 39 & 6:61 and following & 12:42; Romans 9:32 & 10:14 and following; 2 Corinthians 4:4; 1 Timothy 6:2, 3.* **Despisers** and rejecters of this, *2 Thessalonians 2:10; Hebrews 2:1 and following & 3:8 & 4:2.* **Deserters**, *1 Timothy 1:19, 20; 2 Timothy 4:3, 4; Hebrews 6:4, 5 & 10:25.* **The sum of this**, *1 Corinthians 5:7; 1 Timothy 3:4, 5; 2 Thessalonians 1:8; 2 Timothy 3:13.*

**Excommunication**, is the separation or exclusion of the obstinate, and as it were, the amputation of putrid members from the body of the Church. Those who among the Jews were <term>ἀποσυνάγωγος</term> <gloss>cast out of the synagogue</gloss>, *John 9:34.* Concerning this separation, *Matthew 18:17 and following; 1 Corinthians 5:2, 3, 11; 2 Corinthians 2:3; 2 Thessalonians 3:14; 1 Timothy 1:20.*

**Military Service**, <term>στρατεύματα</term> <gloss>armies</gloss> and <term>στρατεύεσθαι</term> <gloss>to serve as a soldier</gloss>, *Matthew 22:7; Luke 21:20.* <term>στρατεία</term> <gloss>warfare</gloss> however, *Luke 2:13.* they have interpreted as Military Service <note>original: "Militia"</note>.

**Exorcists**, a Greek name, among the Jews referring to a singular thing and action, by which by invoking the name of God some might free those who were infected by impure spirits. And there is in the word a meaning of swearing; the Latins began to use the word "Adjuring" for this, *Acts 19:13.*

# INDEX OF WORDS AND PLACES.

**Column 1:**

->F.<-

**Fables**, idle, futile, and fictional stories which must be avoided by those teaching in the Church, *2 Timothy 4:7; 2 Peter 1:16.* They are not to be listened to, *2 Timothy 1:4 <note>The original cites 1 Timothy 1:4 as 2 Timothy 1:4.</note>; Titus 1:14.* Those turning themselves toward such things, *2 Timothy 4:4.*

**Family.** This refers to the household—that is, those who are in anyone’s home, or one's own kin, for whom care must be provided, *1 Timothy 3:12 & 5:4.*

**Feast** is a time and a festive day, the observation of holidays, among which was every seventh day, which they call the Sabbath, *Matthew 12:1, 2, 5; Mark 2:23, 24, 27; Galatians 4:10; Colossians 2:16.*

**The Faithful**, those who believe the Gospel and offer faith to God, who are also the elect, *Matthew 20:16 & 22:14 & 24:24; Luke 18:8, 14; Ephesians 1:1; Colossians 3:12; 1 Thessalonians 1:4; 2 Timothy 2:10; Titus 1:1; 1 Peter 1:1 & 2:9.* **Sons of God**, *John 1:12; Romans 8:33; 2 Corinthians 6:13; Galatians 3:26 & 4:5, 6; Hebrews 2:10.* Disciples are called **Little children** by Christ, *John 13:33.* And **Son**, that is, <note>original: "vi." likely "namely"</note> the paralytic, *Matthew 9:2.* And **Daughter** who is healed, *Matthew 9:22; Mark 5:34.* **Daughter of the kingdom**, *Matthew 13:8.* **Sons of Abraham**, *Romans 4:12, 16, 18; Galatians 3:7.* **Sons of light**, *John 3:6; Ephesians 5:8.* **Heirs of God**, *Romans 8:17; Galatians 4:7; Ephesians 3:6; Titus 3:7; James 2:5.* **Those deemed worthy of the resurrection** do not die, *Luke 20:36.* **Brothers of Christ**, *Matthew 25:40 & 28:10; John 20:17; Romans 8:29; Hebrews 2:11.* **Co-heirs with Christ**, *Romans 8:17.* **A new creature**, *2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15.* **Temple and dwelling-place of God**, *1 Corinthians 3:16, 17; 2 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 2:22.* **Members of God's household**, *Ephesians 2:29.* **Stewards**, *1 Peter 4:10.* **Temple of the Holy Spirit**, *1 Corinthians 6:19.* **The Anointed**, *2 Corinthians 1:21; 1 John 2:20.* **Sealed by the Holy Spirit**, *Ephesians 1:13 & 4:30.* **Having the Holy Spirit as a guide**, *John 6:63; Romans 8:5 and following; Galatians 4:6 & 5:18, 22, 25.* **Saints**, *Acts 9:13; Romans 1:7 & 8:27 & 12:13 & 15:25, 26; 1 Corinthians 6:1, 2 & 14:33 & 16:1; 2 Corinthians 1:1 & 8:4 & 13:12; Ephesians 1:31 & 4:12 & 5:3 & 6:18; Philippians 1:1 & 4:21, 22; Colossians 1:2; 1 Thessalonians 5:27; 1 Timothy 5:10; Titus 1:8; Philemon 5; Hebrews 3:1 & 13:24; 1 Peter 2:9; Jude 3; Revelation 17:6.* **The Just**, *Romans 1:17 & 6:19 & 10:3, 4, 5.* **The Pure**, and those for whom all things are pure, *Titus 1:15.* **All one body of Christ**, *John 17:11; **Faith** carries the meaning of certain, undoubted persuasion and firm trust in those believing the word of God and trusting in His promises. It also signifies the confession of truth and a holy way of life according to it, *John 12:42 & 14:1; Ephesians 1:13 & 4:13; Hebrews 11:1 and following; 1 Peter 1:8.* This is one, *Ephesians 4:5.* The work and gift of God, *Matthew 13:11 & 16; John 6:29; Acts 17:31; Ephesians 1:16, 17 and following & 2:8; 1 Thessalonians 2:3; Philippians 1:29; 2 Peter 1:1; 1 John 5:4, 20.* It is from hearing, *Romans 10:17.* It ought to be certain and firm, *Matthew 20:30, 32; Mark 11:22, 23; Ephesians 3:12; Colossians 1:23 & 2:5, 7; Hebrews 10:35.* It makes us sons of God, *John 1:12; Galatians 3:26.* By this we are given life, justified, purified, reborn, and sanctified, *Luke 7:50; John 3:16 & 5:24 & 6:40 & 11:25 & 20:31; Acts 10:43 & 13:39 & 15:9 & 16:31 & 26:

<column-break/>

**Column 2:**

*18; Romans 1:17 & 3:22, 25 & 4:5 & 5:1 & 9:30 & 10:9; Galatians 2:16 & 3:8; Philippians 3:9; Colossians 1:2, 23; 1 John 5:4, 5 and following.* Without this, no one can please God, *Hebrews 11:6.* Without this, all things are sin, *Romans 14:23.* By this the Holy Spirit is received, *Galatians 3:2, and following.* By this the Gentiles were grafted in, *Romans 11:17, 19, 24.* This is the victory over the world, *1 John 5:14 <note>The Latin text likely refers to 1 John 5:4.</note>.* By this we have peace with God, *Romans 5:1.* By this all things can be done, *Matthew 17:20 & 21:22; Mark 9:23, 24; Luke 17:6; Philippians 5:13 <note>The Latin text likely refers to Philippians 4:13.</note>.* The end of this is the salvation of souls, *1 Peter 1:9.* Through this, Christ dwells in us, *Ephesians 3:17.* By this, the Devil is resisted, *1 Peter 5:7 <note>Likely 1 Peter 5:8-9.</note>; Ephesians 6:16.* By this, people are healed, *Matthew 8:13 and following & 9:6 and following & 15:28; Mark 9:25; Luke 8:48 and following; Acts 3:7 & 14:8, 9.* The many virtues of this, *Hebrews 11:3, 4, 5 and following.* Examples of faith, *Matthew 8:3, 13 & 15:22, 30 and following; Luke 7:10 & 8:44; Romans 4:3 and following; 1 Thessalonians 1:3, 8; Hebrews 1, 1, 2; James 5:17.* It is declared by works, *James 2:14; Philemon 5, 7; 1 John 2:9, 10, 11.* Without works, it is dead, *James 2:17.* Faith must be confessed and an account given for it, *1 Peter 3:15.*

**Confidence** is trust, *Matthew 14:27; John 16:33.* Have confidence, <note>original: "παρρησία" (parrēsia) - boldness or plainness of speech</note>, *Acts 4:13 & 19:8; 2 Corinthians 3:4 & 7:4; Ephesians 3:12; Philippians 1:1, 20; 1 Timothy 3:13; Hebrews 3:6 & 4:6 & 10:19; 1 John 2:28. Boldness. Philippians 3:4.*

**Son**, offspring, *Matthew 13:55 & 21:6, 28.* **Sons of this age**, and **sons of light**, *Luke 16:8 & 20:34.* **Sons of the promise**, *Galatians 4:28.* **Sons of wrath**, *Ephesians 2:3.* **Son of Man**, is a man, and a distinguished title by which the Son of God uses for Himself, our Lord Jesus Christ, true man, *Matthew 24:27, 30, 37 & 25:31 & 26:2.*

**Female**, or woman, made for the man's sake, from the man, *1 Corinthians 11:9.* **Adornment of women**, *1 Timothy 2:9; 1 Peter 3:3.* These ought to be subject to their husbands, *1 Peter 3:1, 5; 1 Corinthians 14:34.* Honor should be held for them by the men, *1 Peter 3:7.* They should not teach in the Church, *1 Corinthians 14:34; 1 Timothy 2:12.* **Ministers** in the Church, whom they called deaconesses, *1 Timothy 3:11.* **Servants of the Church**, *Romans 16:3; 1 Timothy 5:9.*

**Brothers.** This name, according to the custom of the Hebrew language, signifies the entire kinship, *Mark 3:31, 32; Luke 18:19.* Christ calls his own "brothers," *Matthew 28:10; John 20:17; Hebrews 2:11.* All Christ's faithful are **Brothers**, *Matthew 23:8; Romans 1:13 & 8:12 & 12:1; 1 Corinthians 6:8 & 8:12, 13 & 15:1 & 16:12, 14, 20; Ephesians 6:10.* **Brothers to be loved**, *Romans 12:10; 1 Peter 1:22 & 2:17 & 3:8.* Not to be defrauded, *1 Thessalonians 4:6.* Not to be offended, *Romans 14:13; 1 Corinthians 8:13.* He who hates his brother is in darkness, *1 John 2:9.* And a murderer, *1 John 3:13 <note>Original likely refers to 1 John 3:15.</note>.*

**Fraud**, deceit, to defraud, *Mark 10:19; Romans 1:29; Ephesians 4:31; 1 Thessalonians 4:6; 1 Timothy 3:8.*

**Fruit**, the product of stems and trees. A **good tree** bears good fruit, *Matthew 7:17.* **To bear fruit**, *Matthew 13:23; Romans 7:4, 5.* And it signifies actions of <note>original: "μετανοίας" (metanoias) - repentance</note> and those things which are done by all, which are perceived, *Romans 6:21.* **Fruit of the Spirit**, *Galatians 5:22.* **Fruits worthy of repentance**, *Matthew 3:8.* Without fruit, *Matthew 13:22.* **Fruit of the womb** is the blessed offspring of the Virgin Mary, *Luke 1, 42.*

**Flight** from danger is permitted, *Matthew 2:13 & 10:23; Acts 14:6.*

**Thieves**, *Matthew 6:20; Mark 7:22; John 12:6; Romans 13:9; 1 Corinthians 6:10; Ephesians 4:28; 1 Peter 4:15.*

->G.<-

**Joy.** **Joy of the angels**, *Luke 15:10.* **Good joy**, *Luke 6:23.* **Evil joy**, *Luke 6:24 & 12:45, 46 & 16:15, 25; John 16:20; James 4:9; 2 Peter 2:13.*

**Generation**, <note>original: "γένεσις" (genesis) - birth/origin</note>, *Matthew 1:1, 17.* <note>original: "γέννημα" (gennēma) - offspring/product</note>, *Luke 22:18 & Luke 1:7.* **Offspring**, <note>original: "γεννήματα" (gennēmata)</note> or age/generation, *Matthew 2:17 <note>Likely Matthew 3:7.</note> & 24:34; Colossians 1:26.* **The bearing of children**, *2 Timothy 2:15.*

**Gentiles**, nations other than the Jews, idolaters, whose life is not to be followed, *Ephesians 4:7, 11.* To whom also the Gospel is preached and the sheepfold of Christ is opened, *Acts 14:6 and following & 28:13, 14, 23; John 10:16.* They are purified by faith, *Acts 15:9.* They are converted to life, *Acts 11:1.* They know the secrets of grace, *Colossians 1:25, 26.* These are also called Greeks, because that nation was the most famous among the Gentiles.

**Sword of the Spirit**, <note>original: "μάχαιρα" (machaira)</note>, see the word **God**. It signifies affliction and pain, *Luke 2:35.* **Turmoil and discord**, *Matthew 10:34.* **The sword committed to Magistrates**, *Romans 13:4.* Forbidden to private persons, *Matthew 5:22, 23 & 26:52; Revelation 13:10.*

**Glory**, fame and celebration: **To Glorify**, to celebrate. **Glory to God** through Christ and in Christ, *Luke 2:14; Romans 16:27; Acts 13:48; Philippians 4:19, 20; Jude 1:5; 2 Peter 4:16 <note>Likely 1 Peter 4:16.</note>; Revelation 4:11.* All things ought to tend toward glorifying God, *Matthew 5:17; 1 Corinthians 10:13; Colossians 3:17.* **Glory to God**, *Romans 11:36; Galatians 1:5; Ephesians 3:21; 1 Peter 4:11.* **To be glorified in the Lord**, *Romans 5:11; 1 Corinthians 1:31 & 3:21; 2 Corinthians 1:12 & 10:17; Philippians 3:19, 20; Galatians 6:14; Ephesians 3:13.*

# INDEX OF WORDS AND PLACES

Self-glory, forbidden, *Job 5:44; Ephesians 2:9.* Vain glory, *Matthew 23:6, 12; 1 Corinthians 3:4, 5 & following; 2 Corinthians 5:12; Galatians 5:26; Philippians 2:3.*
**Grace**, kindness, favor, and free mercy. The grace of God, *2 Corinthians 6:1; Titus 2:11 & 3:25.* Through Christ and the grace of Christ, *John 1:16; Romans 3:7 & 5:21; 1 Corinthians 1:4; Ephesians 1:2 & 2:7; 2 Timothy 1:9; 2 Peter 3:18.* Through this comes salvation and righteousness, *Acts 15:11; Romans 11:5; Ephesians 2:8; 2 Thessalonians 2:16; Titus 2:11, 12.* In this one must trust, *1 Peter 1:13.* It is lost when trusting in another <note>Meaning trusting in works or other means of salvation rather than grace.</note>, *Galatians 5:4.* Thanks should be given for food and all things, *Matthew 14:19 & 15:36 & 26:26; Acts 27:35; 1 Timothy 4:3; Ephesians 5:4; 1 Thessalonians 5:17.*

### H.

**Inheritance**, immortal, *1 Peter 1:4.* Of the Kingdom of God, *Matthew 25:21; Galatians 3:18.*
**Heir**. Christ is the heir of all things, *Hebrews 1:2;* and in the parable of the vineyard, *Matthew 21:38; Mark 12:7; Luke 20:14.* Believers are his co-heirs, *Romans 8:17; Galatians 4:3, 7; Ephesians 3:6; Titus 3:7.*
**Heresy**, a Greek name signifying a sect <note>original: "sectam"</note>. In Church language, it is the name for an atrocious crime—that is, a falling away from the truth of the universal consensus <note>original: "consensus Catholici," referring here to the general, historic agreement of the Christian church rather than the Roman Catholic denomination specifically.</note> by a turbulent faction; and from this come **Heretics**, who are to be avoided, *1 Corinthians 11:18, 19; 2 Timothy 2:16, 17; Titus 3:9, 10; 2 Peter 2:1, 2 & following.*
**Hallelujah**, two Hebrew words which common pronunciation has joined together, by which meaning God is commanded to be praised. It is retained, however, as a unique form of the Hebrew tongue in these and other words, such as Amen and Hosanna, *Revelation 19:1.*
**Holocaust**, a Greek name <note>original: "Holocaustum," meaning "burnt whole."</note> signifying a certain kind of sacrifice in which the victims were entirely burned up; this was the principal and extraordinary sacrifice among the Jews. Burnt offerings, *Matthew 12:7; Hebrews 10:6.*
**Homicide** (Murder), *Romans 1:29.* Forbidden, *Matthew 5:22 & 19:18; Romans 13:9; Galatians 5:21; 1 Timothy 1:9; 1 Peter 4:15; 1 John 3:15; Revelation 21:8 & 22:15.* It comes forth from the heart and the mouth, *Matthew 15:18, 19.* He who hates his brother is a murderer, *1 John 3:15.*
**Man**, Earthly, *1 Corinthians 15:47.* The Old Man, *Colossians 3:9; Romans 6:6; Ephesians 4:22.* Fleshly, *John 3:6; Romans 7:14.* Natural (or soulish), *1 Corinthians 2:14.* The Outward Man, in which is the appearance of life spent in this world, *2 Corinthians 4:16.* All men are sinners, *Romans 3:23 & 5:12 & 11:32; Galatians 3:22.* Children of wrath, *Ephesians 2:3.* Evil men, *Matthew 7:11.* Liars, *Romans 3:4.* Subject to weakness and evils, *Acts 14:7.* Death reigned over all, *Romans 5:12; 1 Corinthians 3:22.* The will of man, *2 Peter 3:5.* See the word "Will." God wants all men to be saved, *1 Timothy 2:4.* Mortal, *Hebrews 9:12.* The New Man, *Colossians 3:10; 2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15; Ephesians 2:13 & 4:24.* The Inward Man, in which is the understanding of truth and the care of piety, *Romans 7:22; Ephesians 3:16; 1 Peter 3:4.* Spiritual, *John 3:5, 6; 1 Corinthians 2:15.*
**Honor** toward God and Christ; see the word "Glory." Toward parents, *Matthew 15:4; Mark 7:10; Ephesians 6:1, 2.* Toward Kings and Magistrates, *Romans 13:1 & following; 1 Peter 2:17.* Toward teachers of the Gospel, *Galatians 4:13 & following; 1 Timothy 5:1, 4.* Toward Masters from their servants, *1 Timothy 6:1.* From husbands toward their wives, *1 Peter 3:7.* Toward those to whom it is owed, *Romans 13:7.* Toward all, *1 Peter 2:17.* To outdo one another in honor, *Romans 12:10.*
**Hour**, a certain time. They divided the day and the night into twenty-four spaces, which are twelve hours of the day and as many of the night. By common observation, these are indeed unequal outside the times of the equinoxes: the daytime hours are longest at the summer solstice and shortest in winter. Into this [hour], therefore, all things must now fall, *Matthew 8:13 & 10:3 & following; & 24:36 & 25:13 & 26:40, 45 & 27:45, etc.*
**Hospitality**, *Romans 12:13; Hebrews 13:2 <note>Original cites Hebrews 3:2, likely intended 13:2.</note>; 1 Peter 4:9; 1 Timothy 3:2; Titus 1:8.*
**Host** (Sacrificial Victim), the victim which was slain in sacrifices. A sacrifice for sins, *Hebrews 5:1 & 8:2 & 9:9 & 10:5, 8.* The one true and only sacrifice, *2 Corinthians 5:14; Ephesians 2:13, 16; Hebrews 9:14 & 10:10.* See the word "Christ." Spiritual and of praise, *Romans 12:1; Philippians 2:17 & 4:18; Hebrews 13:15; 1 Peter 2:5.*
**Humility** toward God, *Luke 1:48 & 18:14; James 4:6, 7; 1 Peter 5:6.* Toward men, *Matthew 11:9 & 18:4 & 22:12; Luke 10:16; Romans 12:16; Ephesians 4:2; Philippians 2:3; Colossians 3:12; 1 Peter 5:5.*
**Hypocrisy**, a Greek name signifying pretense and a feigned appearance; a thing most hated by God, who is truthful. And **Hypocrites**, the pretenders, *Matthew 6:2 & 7:21 & 15:7, 8 & 22:18 & 23:13 & following; & 24:23; Luke 6:46, 47 & 11:44 & 12:56 & 13:26, 27; Acts 5:1, 2 & following; Colossians 2:18, 23; 1 Timothy 4:2; 2 Timothy 3:5.*

### I.

**Idol**, a Greek name; an image or likeness, and properly signifies the effigies of false deities. And an **Idolater**, one who worships idols: and this crime of impiety, **Idolatry**, *Acts 7:40 &*

<column-break/>

*14:11, 12 & 15:29 & 7:23 <note>Likely Acts 17:23</note> & 19:24 & following; Romans 1:13; 1 Corinthians 5:11 & 6:9 & 8:1, 4 & 10:7, 14 & following; 2 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 5:5; Galatians 5:20; Colossians 3:5; 1 Thessalonians 1:9; 1 Peter 4:3; Revelation 2:14 & 9:20 & 22:15.*
**Fasting**, *Matthew 6:16 & following; & 9:14 & 17:21; Luke 5:33 & following; Acts 13:2 & 14:22; 1 Corinthians 7:3; 2 Corinthians 6:5.*
**Ignorance** of God, *Acts 17:23; Romans 10:3; Ephesians 4:18.* Ignorance which has forgiveness, *Acts 3:17; Galatians 4:8; 1 Timothy 1:13.* Destructive ignorance, *2 Thessalonians 1:8, 9; 1 Timothy 1:6, 7; 2 Peter 2:12; Jude 10.*
**Mockers** and despisers of the Gospel, *Acts 13:2 <note>Likely Acts 13:41</note> & 17:5; 2 Peter 3:3; Jude 18.* Against contempt, *Matthew 18:24 with following.*
**Image** of God: Christ is, *2 Corinthians 4:4; Colossians 1:15; Hebrews 1:3.* Man is, *1 Corinthians 11:7; Colossians 3:10.* Man as the image of Christ, *Romans 8:30; 1 Corinthians 15:49; 2 Corinthians 3:18.*
**Hardening**, which is also blinding, *John 12:40; Acts 7:51 & 13:6 <note>Likely Acts 13:8-11</note>; Romans 9:18 & 10:21 & 11:7.* Certain ones were hardened, *Acts 19:28 & following.*
**Infancy** of Christ, *Hebrews 5:2; 1 Peter 1:14.* <note>These references likely refer to Christ's humility or identifying with human weakness rather than literal childhood stories.</note>
**Hell**, truly a place; called *Hades* among the Greeks, and *Gehenna* among the Hebrews. Unquenchable fire, *Matthew 3:10 & 5:22 & 10:28 & 18:9 & 25:41; Mark 9:43; Luke 3:17 & 10:15 & 12:5; Acts 2:24; Philippians 2:10; Jude 7; Revelation 6:8 & 20:10.* The worm that does not die, *Mark 9:44.* Darkness, *Matthew 8:12 & 22:13 & 25:30.* Where there is weeping and groaning, in the same place.
**Weak** in faith, *Romans 14:1 & 15:1; 1 Thessalonians 5:14; 1 Corinthians 8:9, 11 & 9:22.* God chose the weak, *1 Corinthians 1:27.*
**Injury** and violence to be endured, *Matthew 5:9; 1 Corinthians 6:7.*
**Disobedience**, *Romans 1:30 & 5:19; 2 Thessalonians 1:8 & 3:14; 2 Timothy 3:2; Colossians 3:20; 2 Peter 2:10; Jude 8.*
**Envy**, rivalry, *Acts 4:2 & 5:18 & 17:5; Romans 1:29; Galatians 5:20, 21; 1 Timothy 6:4; Titus 3:3; James 3:14; 1 Peter 2:1.*
**Wrath** of God is the execution of the just and severe judgment of God in punishing sinners, *John 3:36; Colossians 3:6; 1 Thessalonians 2:16; James 5:3.* Christ has freed us from wrath, *1 Thessalonians 1:10.* One must not be angry, *Matthew 5:23, 44, 45; Romans 12:14; Ephesians 4:26 & 6:4; Colossians 3:8; 1 Timothy 4:9, 10 & 5:14; 2 Timothy 2:14 & 3:10 & 4:14, 15, 16; Titus 3:2.*
**Jews**. Their excellence, *Romans 3:1, 2.* Their blinding, *2 Corinthians 3:14.* Rejected because of unbelief, though not entirely, *Romans 11:23.* Between them and the Gentiles there is no distinction, *Romans 10:12; Galatians 3:28.* The outward and inward Jew, *Romans 2:28, 29.*
**Judgment** of God, *Romans 11:33; Revelation 19:2.* Unsearchable, true, and just, *ibid. John 3:18, 29; Romans 2:6; 1 Corinthians 11:32; 1 Peter 4:5.* The Last Judgment, the time of which is unknown, *Matthew 24:42 & 25:13; Luke 12:40; Romans 2:7; 1 Thessalonians 5:2; 2 Timothy 4:1, 8; Hebrews 9:27; 2 Peter 4:5; James 5:9.* Human judgment, *John 7:12; 1 Corinthians 4:5; James 4:11, 12.*
**Oath** of God, *Luke 1:73; Hebrews 6:13, 14 & 7:20.* Of men, *Hebrews 6:16.* Forbidden, *Matthew 5:35 & following; James 5:12.*
**Righteousness** (or Justice), the righteous man. He who does righteousness is righteous, *1 John 3:7.* The righteous man lives by faith, *Romans 1:17; Hebrews 10:38.*
**Justify**, signifies to declare righteous, or to carry out a legal sentence, *Matthew 11:19 & 12:37; Luke 7:29 & 16:15.* The free absolution from sins for those who believe, *Romans 3:24 & 4:5 & following; & 5:1 & 6:18; 1 Corinthians 6:12; Titus 2:11 & 3:7.* For those wishing to be justified by the Law, Christ died in vain, *Galatians 2:21 & 5:2.* No one can accuse those who are justified, *Romans 8:1.* And according to the doctrine of Paul, that men are justified by faith, he says this: that they are received into grace and declared righteous by the sentence of God for those believing the Gospel on account of the merit and grace of Christ. The righteousness of the Law, and the observation of legal requirements, *Luke 1:16.*

### L.

**Labor**, and to work, to do some kind of work is commanded to all, *1 Thessalonians 4:11; 2 Thessalonians 3:12.* Otherwise let them not eat, *Ephesians 4:28; 2 Thessalonians 3:10.* The example of Paul the Apostle, *Acts 18:3 & 20:4; 1 Corinthians 4:12; 1 Thessalonians 2:9; 2 Thessalonians 3:8.*
**Praise**, *Romans 2:29 & 13:3; 1 Corinthians 4:5; 2 Corinthians 10:17; 1 Peter 2:7; Revelation 5:12, 13 & 19:1.* A sacrifice of praise, *Hebrews 13:15.*
**Legion**, a Latin name which the Greeks also used, for a specific number of troops in the military, approximately 1,000 infantry and 500 cavalry <note>The author's estimate here is lower than a standard Roman legion, which usually contained about 5,000 to 6,000 men.</note>, *Matthew 26:53; Mark 5:9; Luke 8:30.*
**Law** of ceremonies, looking toward the coming of Christ, *Galatians 3:24; Hebrews 10:1.* Abolished, *Ephesians 2:11 & following; Colossians 2:16.* The Moral Law is good, just, and holy, *Romans 7:12; 1 Timothy 1:8 & following.* It is spiritual, *Romans 7:14.* The power—that is, the potency—of sin, *Romans 7:8, 11; 1 Corinthians 15:56.* The administration of death, *2 Corinthians 3:7.* The rigor of the Law, *Hebrews 12:11.* Accursed are those who are under the Law, *Galatians 3:10.* It does not give life, *ibid. 21.* Unbearable, *Acts 15:10.* Increasing transgression and leading to Christ, who freed us from the Law, *Romans 4:15 & 8:2; Galatians 3:19 & 4:31.* Christ is the end of the Law, *Romans 10:4.* The Law written in the hearts of the faithful, *Romans 7:21, 23; Hebrews 8:10.* The summary of the Law, *Matthew 22:40; Romans 13:8 & following; Galatians 5:14.* One lawgiver, *James 4:12.*
