# INDEX of WORDS and PLACES.

**Certificate of divorce** <note>original: "Libellus repudii"</note>. The Romans called it a formal notice <note>original: "nuncium"</note>, which is the dismissing of a wife. This is granted in the case of adultery, *Matthew 5:32-33 & 19:7; Mark 10:4 & following; Luke 16:8; 1 Corinthians 7:27.*

**Children**. Their duty, *Ephesians 6:1 & following; Colossians 3:20.*

**Spiritual liberty**, *John 8:33, 34; Acts 15:28, 29; Romans 6:20, 21 & 8:12; 2 Corinthians 3:6; Galatians 2:4 & 3:25, 28 & 5:1 & following; Ephesians 2:19; Colossians 2:16.* Regarding matters of indifference <note>original: "Rerum differentium," referring to things neither commanded nor forbidden by God</note>, *Romans 14:2, 3 & following; 1 Corinthians 10:3; 1 Timothy 4:3; Titus 1:15.* To be preserved, *Matthew 15:3 & following; Galatians 5:14.* Must serve charity <note>or "love"</note>, *1 Corinthians 9:9, 10 & 10:32; Galatians 5:6.* Carnal liberty, ibid. *13, 19; 1 Peter 2:11; 2 Peter 2:18.*

**Tongue**. The nature of this, *James 3:5, 6 & following.* To be kept from evil, *1 Peter 3:10.* See the word, **Slander**. Different tongues <note>the gift of speaking in languages</note>, *Mark 16:18; Acts 2:6, 7 & 19:6; 2 Corinthians 12:10.* A known language is to be used in the Church, *1 Corinthians 14:5, 6.*

**The letter** is opposed to the spirit, *Romans 2:29; 1 Corinthians 3:9.*

**Legal lawsuits** to be avoided, *Matthew 5:40; 1 Corinthians 6:1, 2.*

### M

**Magi**, wise men of the East, from Arabia, according to Justin, *Matthew 2:1.* Superstitious men and enchanters, *Acts 8:9, 11 & 13:6.*

**Magistrates**, divinely ordained, *Romans 13:1, 2 & following; 1 Peter 2:14.* To them obedience and honor are owed, *ibid. 17; Titus 3:1.* Tribute must be paid, *Luke 20:25; Romans 13:6.* Prayer should be made for them, *1 Timothy 2:1, 2.*

**Cursing** of the mouth, *Romans 3:14; James 3:10.* The curse of the Law, *Galatians 3:10, 11, 13.* Christ freed us from the curse of the Law, having been made a curse, *Galatians 3:13.*

**Slanderers** <note>or "revilers"</note>, *1 Corinthians 5:11 & 6:10; Jude 8.* Blessing is to be given to those who curse, *Luke 6:28; 1 Peter 3:9.* Following the example of Christ and Paul, *1 Corinthians 4:12.* On those who are cursed because of Christ, *Matthew 5:11.* Persecutors are not to be cursed, *Romans 12:14.*

**Evil** comes forth from the heart, *Matthew 12:34 & 15:18 & following; Mark 7:21, 22, 23.* To be held in hatred, *Romans 12:9.* Not to be repaid; see the word, **Vengeance**.

**Commandment** of God, *Matthew 5:20 & 15:3 & following & 19:17 & 22:36; Mark 7:8; John 12:49 & 13:34 & 14:15 & 15:10; Romans 7:8 & 13:9; 1 Corinthians 7:10; 1 John 2:3 & 3:23 & 4:21; 2 John 4, 6, 7; Revelation 12:17.* Commandment of men, *Matthew 15:2; Mark 7:5, 7; Luke 11:46; Ephesians 4:17, 18; Colossians 2:8; 1 Timothy 4:1, 2; Titus 1:14.*

**Hand**, a part of the body, *Matthew 3:12 & 8:3 & 9:18 & 26:23; Mark 3:1.* The carrying out, the result, and the work, *Luke 22:53; Acts 13:11 & 19:11; Galatians 3:19; 1 Peter 5:6.*

**Sea**, also signifies large lakes, such as the Sea of Tiberias, *John 6:1 & 21:1.*

**Mary**, Virgin, Mother of Jesus Christ, Handmaid of God, *Luke 1, 11, 27, 31, 38.* Blessed, *Luke 1:28 & 11:27.*

**Matrimony** or marriage, the lawful union of a male and female, *Matthew 19:4; 1 Corinthians 7:2 & following.* Divinely ordained, *Matthew 19:4.* Forbidden to no one, *1 Corinthians 7:36 & following; 1 Timothy 3:2, 3; Titus 1:6.* Honorable, *Hebrews 13:4.* Necessary for those without self-control, *Matthew 19:11 & following; 1 Corinthians 7:2.* It is honored by the presence of Christ, *John 2:2, 3.* Compared with the union of Christ and the Church, *Ephesians 5:22, 23 & following.* Chaste, *1 Peter 3:2.* It must not be torn apart by men, *Matthew 19:6.* The life of spouses, *1 Corinthians 7:3, 10 & 11:4 & following; Ephesians 5:24, 25; Colossians 3:18, 19; 1 Timothy 2:8, 9 & following; Titus 2:2, 3, 4 & following; 1 Peter 3:1 & following.* Dissolved only in the case of adultery, *Matthew 5:33 & 19:9.* The deserted one is free, *1 Corinthians 7:39, 40.*

**Mediator**, *Galatians 3:20.* One Mediator of God and men, *1 Timothy 2:5; Hebrews 8:6 & 9:15 & 12:24.*

**Members**, parts of the body, *Romans 6:13 & 7:5; Colossians 3:3.* <term>ta melē</term> <note>original Greek: "τα μέλη"</note>, those who fill up some community, as if a body, *Romans 12:4; 1 Corinthians 6:15 & 12:12.*

**Lying** is from the Devil, *John 8:44.* Prohibited, *Ephesians 4:25; Colossians 3:9; James 3:14.* It signifies the total perversity of man, *Romans 3:4, 7.*

**Liar**. Every man is a liar, *Romans 3:4.* A liar is one not confessing that he is a sinner, *1 John 1:8.* He who says he knows God and does not keep his commandments, *1 John 2:4.* He who denies that Jesus is the Christ, ibid. 22. He who says he loves God and hates his brother, *1 John 4:20.* Those persevering in a lie are condemned, *Revelation 21:8.*

**Beggars** <note>original: "Mendicantes"</note>, not to be tolerated, *2 Thessalonians 3:10, 11 & following.* All ought to do some work. See the word, **Labor**. So that none are burdened, *Matthew 23:4, 5; 2 Corinthians 11:9; 1 Thessalonians 2:7; 2 Thessalonians 3:8; 1 Timothy 5:16.*

**Ministry** of the word of God, which is the proclamation of the Gospel, *Acts 20:24.*

**Ministers**, and their office, *Acts 6:2, 3; 1 Timothy 3:8, 12.*

**Female minister** <note>or Deaconess; original: "Ministra"</note>, *Romans 16:1, 2 & following.*

**Miracle**. True miracles confirm divine power, *Matthew 11:5, 20; Mark 16:17; John 5:36 & 10:25 & 20,*

<column-break/>

*30, 31; Acts 2:43 & 4:22 & 14:3; 2 Corinthians 12:12; Hebrews 2:4.* They are not done by human virtue, but by the divine virtue of Christ, *Acts 3:12, 13 & 4:10 & 9:34.* False miracles, pertaining to errors and lies, *Matthew 24:24; Mark 13:22; 2 Thessalonians 2:9; Revelation 13:13, 14 & 16:14.*

**Mercy of God** through Christ, *Luke 1:50, 72, 78; Hebrews 4:16; 1 Timothy 1:2; 1 Peter 1:3; Ephesians 2:4.* Through this, salvation, *Titus 3:5; 1 Peter 1:3.* Pertaining to the Gentiles, *Romans 11:30, 31 & 15:9.* To those who fear God, *Luke 1:50.* To those who are converted, *Luke 15:20.* To the faithful, *2 Corinthians 4:1, 2; 1 Peter 2:10.* Precepts, *Luke 6:36; Ephesians 4:32; Colossians 3:12; 1 Peter 3:8.* God wants this, and not sacrifice, *Matthew 9:13 & 12:7.* Among the weightier commandments, *Matthew 23:23.* Blessed are the merciful, *Matthew 5:7.* God has mercy on whom he has mercy, *Romans 9:5.* For the one not showing mercy, judgment is without mercy, *James 2:13.*

**Monument** <note>or Memorial/Tomb</note>, has the meaning in the Gospel writings, as also in others, of a **Sepulcher**, by which the memory of the dead is preserved, *Matthew 27:60; Mark 15:46; Luke 23:53, 55; John 19:41.*

**Disease**, a punishment for sins, *John 5:14; 2 Corinthians 11:30.* Sometimes pertaining to the glory of God, *John 9:3 & 11:4.* Those laboring under diseases are to be comforted, *Matthew 25:36, 43.*

**Death** of the body is common to all, *1 Corinthians 15:5; Hebrews 9:27.* It does not separate us from the grace of God, *Romans 8:38.* Desired by the Apostle, *Philippians 1:23.* The dead are said to sleep, *Matthew 9:24; Acts 7:60 & 13:36; 1 Corinthians 11:30; 1 Thessalonians 4:13.* Death destroyed through Christ, *2 Timothy 1:10; Hebrews 2:14, 15.* It serves us, *1 Corinthians 3:22.* The dead do not teach, *Luke 16:29, 31.* The faithful dead are blessed, *Revelation 14:13.* They are with God and with Christ, *Luke 23:43; 2 Corinthians 5:1; Philippians 1:21, 23.* The unfaithful dead are in hell, *Luke 16:22.*

**Mortification** of ourselves, *Colossians 3:5.* That is, to die to sin, *Romans 6:2.* It signifies the cross, *Romans 8:13.* Example of Christ, *2 Corinthians 4:10.*

**Woman**, see the word, **Female**.

**The World** was made through Christ, yet did not know Christ, *John 1:10.* Nor God, *John 17:25.* It is entirely placed in the power of the evil one, *1 John 5:19.* It has the Devil as its prince, *Matthew 4:8, 9; Luke 4:6; John 12:31 & 14:30 & 16:11.* Christ does not pray for this, *John 17:9.* Conquered by Christ, *John 16:33.* Faith conquers it, *1 John 5:4.* Whatever is in it is the lust of the flesh and of the eyes, *1 John 2:16.* It passes away, ibid. 17; *1 Corinthians 7:31.* In one who loves the world, the love of God is not there, *1 John 2:15; James 4:4.* The world hates Christ and Christians, *John 7:7 & 15:18; 1 John 3:13.* The faithful are judges of the world, *1 Corinthians 6:2, 3.* Those who are not of the world, *John 17:14.* Worldly lusts are to be fled, *Titus 2:12.*

**Murmur**, and to murmur, that is, to be indignant; prohibited and evil, *Matthew 20:11; Luke 5:30 & 15:2 & 19:7; John 6:41; Acts 6:1; Romans 1:21; 1 Corinthians 10:10; Philippians 2:14; 1 Peter 4:9; Jude 16.*

### N

**Business affairs** <note>referring to legal disputes</note>, lawsuit, contention, debate, questions, fights; to be fled, *Romans 1:29 & 2:7, 8 & 13:4 & 14:1 & following & 16:17; 1 Corinthians 1:12 & 3:3, 4 & 6:3 & 11:17 & 12:15 & following; Galatians 5:18; 1 Timothy 1:9, 10 & 3:8 & 6:4; 2 Timothy 2:12; Titus 3:3, 4; James 3:6 & 4:1 & following.*

**Name of the Lord**, *Acts 2:21; Romans 2:24 & 10:13.* Name of Christ, *Acts 4:10; Philippians 2:10.*

### O

**Obedience**, <term>hypakoē & hypotagē</term> <note>original Greek: "υπακοή & υποταγή"</note>, that is, submission; is owed to God more than to men, *Acts 5:29.* Obedience of faith, *Romans 1:5 & 16:26; 2 Corinthians 9:13; 1 Peter 1:12.* Obedience of wives toward husbands, *1 Peter 3:1 & following.*

**Slander** <note>or detraction</note>, *2 Corinthians 12:2; James 4:11; 1 Peter 2:16.* To stand in the way <note>or hinder</note>, *1 Peter 2:1.*

**Idleness**, an idle word spoken, *Matthew 12:36.* Against idleness, *2 Thessalonians 3:8, 9 & following; 1 Timothy 5:13.*

**Hatred of the world** against Christ and Christians, see the words, **Christ** and **The Faithful**. Hatred of the vice, not of the person, *Jude 23.* Prohibited, *Matthew 5:44; Galatians 5:14, 15; Titus 3:2; 1 John 2:10 & 3:10 & following.*

**Good works** are from God, *Philippians 1:6 & 2:13; Colossians 1:10; Titus 2:7; Hebrews 13:21.* They accompany faith, *Luke 19:8, 9; Hebrews 11:4, 5 & following.* They are done by the good, *Matthew 7:2, 16 & 12:35; Luke 6:45.* They are fruits of the Spirit, *Galatians 5:22; Ephesians 5:9.* In which the faithful ought to walk, *Ephesians 2:9 & 5:8, 9; Titus 2:7, 12 & 3:8, 14; Hebrews 10:24; 1 Peter 2:12.* They are a testimony of repentance, *Acts 26:20.* The judgment of faith, *Luke 19:8; Titus 1:12, 13; James 2:14, 15 & following.* They confirm calling and election, *2 Peter 1:10.* They are not the cause of justification before God, *Romans 4:2 & following & 11:6; Ephesians 2:9; 2 Timothy 1:9; Titus 3:5.* They pertain to the glory of God, *Matthew 5:17; 1 Peter 2:12.* They follow the dead,

# INDEX of WORDS and PLACES.

...your [works], *Revelation* 14:13. They have their reward, *Matthew* 10:41, 42 & 16:27 & 25:46; *Luke* 5:27 & 14:14; *John* 5:29; *1 Corinthians* 2:9 & 15:58; *Galatians* 6:9, 10; *Revelation* 2:26, 27. There are no good works without faith, *John* 15:4, 5; *Romans* 14:22, 23; *Hebrews* 11:6. The evils of the flesh, *Galatians* 5:19 & following. Things that defile men, *Matthew* 15:18, 19. The Devil is the author of these, *Ephesians* 2:2. Christus came that he might destroy them, *1 John* 3:8. They are to be cast away, *Romans* 13:12, 13; *Ephesians* 4:22 & 5:2, 3; *1 Peter* 4:15.

**Prayer** <note>original: "Oratio"</note>, these are spiritual petitions, *Matthew* 6:7; *Job* 4:24; *Romans* 8:15; *Ephesians* 6:17, 18; *Jude* 20. One who prays in faith obtains, *Matthew* 21:22; *Mark* 11:24; *John* 15:7; *James* 1:5 & 5:16 & following; *1 John* 5:14, 15. One must pray in the name of Christ, *John* 14:14 & 15:16. Without ceasing and everywhere, *Matthew* 7:7, 8; *Luke* 11:9 & 18:1 & 21:36; *Acts* 1:14 & 2:42; *Romans* 12:12; *Ephesians* 6:18; *Colossians* 4:2; *1 Thessalonians* 5:17; *1 Timothy* 2:8 & 5:5; *1 Peter* 4:7. In secret, *Matthew* 6:6 & 14:23 & 26:36; *Luke* 5:16 & 6:12 & 22:41; *Acts* 10:9. With thanksgiving, *2 Corinthians* 1:11; *Philippians* 4:6; *Colossians* 1:9. By this, all things are sanctified, *1 Timothy* 4:5. One should pray for another, *James* 5:16. To pray for the saints <note>referring to fellow believers</note>, *Romans* 15:30; *Ephesians* 6:18; *Colossians* 4:12; *2 Thessalonians* 3:1; *Hebrews* 13:18. For the teachers of the Gospel, *Matthew* 9:38; *Luke* 10:2; *Acts* 4:29; *Romans* 15:30; *2 Corinthians* 1:11; *Ephesians* 6:18; *Colossians* 4:3; *2 Thessalonians* 3:1. For kings and powers, *1 Timothy* 2:1. For enemies, *Matthew* 5:44; *Luke* 23:34; *Acts* 7:60. For everyone, *1 Timothy* 2:1. Against temptations, *Matthew* 26:41; *Luke* 22:46. Prayer with fasting, *Matthew* 17:21; *Luke* 2:37; *Acts* 13:3 & 14:22; *1 Corinthians* 7:5. Public prayers, *Acts* 2:42 & 3:1 & 4:24 & 12:5 & 13:22 & 16:16 & 20:36 & 21:5; *1 Timothy* 2:1. In a known language, *1 Corinthians* 14:13, 14. The form of prayer, *Matthew* 6:9; *Luke* 11:2. The power of prayer, *Matthew* 21:22; *John* 15:7; *James* 5:15. To pray in affliction, *Matthew* 26:39; *Luke* 22:39 & following; *Acts* 7:50, 60 & 12:5, 12; *Romans* 15:30, 31; *James* 5:13 & following.

**Ostentation & boasting**, *Luke* 18:11; *Romans* 1, 29; *2 Corinthians* 11, 18 & following.

->P.<-

**Bread** <note>original: "Panis"</note>. The "Loaves of Proposition" <note>the Showbread</note> were so-called and were among the Jews XII in number, which were set out in the temple every VII days, or weeks, and were changed, as is read in *Leviticus* 24:5. The word signifies human food, *Matthew* 6:11. Multiplied loaves, *Matthew* 14:20; *Mark* 6:43; *Luke* 9:17; *John* 6:13. Christ is the bread of life, *John* 6:48. The children's bread, *Matthew* 15:26. The blessing of bread, and with this the participation in the body of Christ, *Matthew* 26:26; *Mark* 14:22; *Luke* 22:19; *1 Corinthians* 10:16. Many are one bread and one body, in the same place 17.

**Paradise,** a Greek word signifying excellent gardens, and the eternal pleasantness of the blessed life, *Luke* 23:43.

**I spare** <note>original: "Parco"</note>, *1 Corinthians* 7:28. Not sparing, *Acts* 20:29.

**Parents** are to be honored, *Matthew* 15:4; *Mark* 7:10; *Luke* 18:20; *Ephesians* 6:1; *Colossians* 3:20; *1 Timothy* 5:4; *Hebrews* 12:7, 8. Not to be loved more than Christ, *Matthew* 10:37. To be left for Christ's sake, *Matthew* 19:29. A man leaves these for the sake of a wife, *Matthew* 19:5; *Ephesians* 5:31.

**Passover** <note>original: "Pascha"</note>, just as the Greeks express the Hebrew word, it has the meaning of "passing over," and of the paschal lamb, and of a solemn feast, *Matthew* 26:2; *Mark* 14:1; *Luke* 22:1; *John* 2:13 & 6:4 & 11:55 & 13:1 & 18:28; *Acts* 12:4; *1 Corinthians* 5:7; *Hebrews* 11:28.

**Shepherd** <term>ποιμήν</term> <note>original: "poimēn"</note>, as also in Greek speech, a governor and presiding leader. Christ the shepherd, *John* 10:11; *Hebrews* 13:20; *1 Peter* 2:25 & 5:4. Shepherds, that is, teachers and presiding leaders in the Church, *Ephesians* 4:11.

**Patience,** necessary for the faithful, *Luke* 21:19; *Romans* 5:3, 4 & 12:12; *1 Corinthians* 4:12; *Colossians* 1:11 & 3:12; *1 Thessalonians* 5:14; *2 Thessalonians* 1:4; *James* 1:3, 4 & 5:7; *1 Peter* 3:14.

**Fathers,** also signifies ancestors, just as sons signify posterity. Their errors are not to be followed, *Matthew* 15:5, 6; *Mark* 7:8, 9; *Luke* 11:47, 48; *Acts* 3:14; *Galatians* 1:14; *1 Peter* 1:14.

**Patriarch,** a Greek word, a primary father or prince, *Acts* 2:29 & 7:8, 9.

**Poor** in spirit, are the humble, *Matthew* 5:3; *Luke* 6:20. To these the Gospel is announced, *Matthew* 11:5. The poor are to be provided for, *Luke* 14:13; *Romans* 12:13 & 15:26, 27; *2 Corinthians* 8:4; *Galatians* 2:10; *Ephesians* 2:28.

**Peace** of God through Christ, *Matthew* 10:12, 13; *Luke* 2:14, 29 & 24:36; *John* 14:27 & 16:33; *Romans* 5:1; *Philippians* 4:7; *Ephesians* 2:14; *Colossians* 1:3 & 3:15. Peace with one's neighbor, *Matthew* 5:9, 26 & following; *Mark* 9:50; *Romans* 12:8 & 15:1, 2; *1 Corinthians* 14:33; *2 Corinthians* 13:11; *Ephesians* 4:2; *1 Thessalonians* 5:13; *2 Thessalonians* 3:16; *2 Timothy* 2:22; *Hebrews* 12:14; *1 Peter* 3:11. Peace of the world, *Matthew* 10:34; *John* 14:27; *1 Thessalonians* 5:13.

**Sinners** are not heard by God, *John* 9:31. They are called to repentance, *Matthew* 9:13; *2 Peter* 3:9.

**Sin** <note>original: "Peccatum"</note>, in all men, *Romans* 3:9 & 5:12.

<column-break/>

& following & 11:32; *Galatians* 3:22; *1 John* 1:8, 10. Knowledge of this through the Law, *Romans* 3:20 & 7:7. It is conquered through Christ, *1 Corinthians* 15:56, 57. It signifies evil desire <note>original: "concupiscentiam"</note> in man, *Romans* 5:12 & following & 6:1, 2 & 7:7 & following. And the fruits of this, *Matthew* 3:10; *1 Corinthians* 6:9 & following; *James* 1:15. Sin is iniquity, *1 John* 3:4. Let not sin reign in us, *Romans* 16:12. Sin is the sting of death, *1 Corinthians* 15:56. Sin unto death, and that which is not forgiven, *Matthew* 12:31; *Mark* 3:28. Not unto death, and that which is forgiven, ibid. Covered sins, *Romans* 4:7. Christ as sin, upon whom the sin of the human race was transferred, and who is the sacrifice for sin, *Romans* 8:2, 3; *2 Corinthians* 5:21.

**Pentecost,** a Greek name, by this is signified the fiftieth day; formerly Jewish holidays, on which the Holy Spirit descended upon the Apostles, *Acts* 2:1 & 20:16; *1 Corinthians* 16:8.

**Persecution,** is the force which is brought by those more powerful, which it is necessary for Christians to endure in the world, *Matthew* 23:34; *Acts* 13:50; *Romans* 8:35; *1 Timothy* 4:11, 12; *2 Timothy* 3:10; *1 Peter* 4:12 & following. Even from one's own relatives, *Matthew* 10:35; *Mark* 13:12; *Luke* 21:16. And they ought to bear this patiently, *Luke* 21:19; *Romans* 12:12; *Hebrews* 10:36. With joy, *Matthew* 5:11, 12; *Acts* 5:41; *1 Peter* 2:20 & 4:14. It is permitted to flee, *Matthew* 2:13, 23; *Acts* 8:1 & 14:6. It happens by the will of God, *1 Peter* 2:19, 20 & 3:17 & 4:19. With whom life is to be placed <note>entrusting one's soul to God</note>, ibid. Some then fall away from the Gospel, *Mark* 4:17. Examples of persecutions, *Matthew* 26:50; *Acts* 4:2, 3 & 5:18 & 12:1, 3 & 7:58 & 8:3 & 9:1 & 12:2 & 13:50 & 14:18 & 16:22 & 17:15 & 18:6 & following & 19:23 & 21:33; *Romans* 8:29; *2 Corinthians* 10:23 & following; *Hebrews* 10:35, 36 & following; *Revelation* 6:9 & 12:13 & 17:6.

**Persecutor,** the author or administrator of such violence. Ignorance in these finds pardon, *Acts* 2:23 & following & 3:14, 17 & 8:3 & 9:1 & 26:10; *1 Timothy* 1:13. The obstinate are punished, *Luke* 23:28, 29; *Acts* 12:23; *Revelation* 6:10, 16, 17.

**Perseverance,** in prayer, *Acts* 1:14; *Luke* 11:9, 10 & 18, & 59. See the word, **Constancy**.

**Person,** an outward appearance, which God does not regard. Respect of persons <note>partiality</note>, *Matthew* 22:16; *Acts* 10:34; *Romans* 2:11; *Galatians* 2:6; *Ephesians* 6:9; *1 Peter* 1:17; *James* 2:5. And he judges individuals, *2 Corinthians* 1:9.

**Philosophy,** a Greek name, the study of wisdom, whose deceptive perversity is to be avoided, *Colossians* 2:8.

**Cup,** see the word, **Chalice**.

**Repentance** <note>original: "Pœnitentia"</note> true, *Matthew* 3:2, 8 & 4:17; *Luke* 3:3, 8 & 13:3; *John* 8:11; *Acts* 2:38 & 3:19 & 5:31 & 17:30 & 20:21 & 26:20; *Romans* 2:4; *2 Peter* 3:9; *Revelation* 2:22. Examples, *Luke* 15:1 & following; *2 Peter* 2:21. An example of destructive repentance <note>the despair of Judas</note>, *Matthew* 27:5.

**Poet,** a Greek name, signifies a maker, especially one who makes verses. This is not read in the Gospel and Apostolic writings, but verses are cited, *Acts* 17:18; *1 Corinthians* 15:33; *Titus* 1:12. God, however, is the eternal Maker, that is, <term>κτίστης</term> <note>original: "ktistēs," Creator</note>, of heaven and earth and all things which are contained in them. Makers of the law and of doctrine, *Romans* 2:13; *James* 1:22 & 4:16, 17.

**Pomp,** pride, adornment, *Mark* 12:26; *Luke* 7:11; *Revelation* 18:1 & following.

**Gates,** <term>μεταφορικῶς</term> <note>original: "metaphorikōs," metaphorically</note>, are the powers of a kingdom, by the custom of Hebrew speech. Of Hell, *Matthew* 16:18. Properly they are of cities, which are also double-doors, *Acts* 9:24; *Revelation* 21:13, 25.

**Power** of God, see the word, **God**, and **Christ**, and **Virtue**. Power of the Magistrate, *Romans* 13:1, 23; *2 Corinthians* 10:8 & 13:10. Power for evil, *Revelation* 9:3.

**To Predestine,** To Pre-define, *Romans* 8:29, 30; *1 Corinthians* 2:7; *Ephesians* 1:5. Predestined, *Romans* 1:4.

**Preaching** <note>original: "Prædicatio"</note> signifies a proclamation, that is, a certain public voice proclaiming something, *Luke* 11:32; *1 Corinthians* 1:21 & 2:4 & 15:14; *2 Timothy* 4:2; *Titus* 1:3. And there are preachers, heralds of heavenly truth and ministers of the word of God. Sent by God, *Matthew* 6:10 & 10:5, 6, 7 & *Romans* 10:15. These ought to teach nothing except what they were commanded by Christ, *Matthew* 28:20; *2 John* 4. Which is the word of God, *1 Corinthians* 1:5, 18 & 2:7; *1 Timothy* 1:11; *1 Peter* 4:5. The example of Christ, *John* 7:16. These are to be heard, *Luke* 10:16. And these must be obeyed, *Matthew* 23:37; *2 Corinthians* 2:8, 9 & 7:14, 15; *Philippians* 2:12; *2 Thessalonians* 3:14; *Hebrews* 13:17. # INDEX of WORDS and PLACES.

<note>This section continues from the previous page's discussion of those who serve in the church.</note> 18. & 4. & 5, 21. Serving others, *Matthew 20:26, 27; Mark 10:43, 44; Luke 22:26; 1 Corinthians 3:5; 2 Corinthians 4:1.* Building upon Christ alone, *1 Corinthians 3:9, 11.* Their power, *2 Corinthians 10:4.* For building up, not destroying, *in the same place & 13:10.* For the truth, not against it, *in the same place, verse 8.* Subject to persecution, *Matthew 10:23.* Their office, *Acts 20:20, 21; 1 Timothy 3:2 and following; Titus 1:7 and following; 1 Peter 5:2 and following.* An example set before others, *Philippians 3:17; 2 Thessalonians 3:9; 1 Timothy 4:12; Titus 2:7; Hebrews 13:7; 1 Peter 5:3.* Appointed in individual churches, *Acts 14:22 & 20:22, 25; Titus 1:5.* Not to be ordained lightly, *in the same place, verse 6 and following.* Prediction concerning false Preachers, and that they must be avoided, *Matthew 7:15 & 16:6 & 24:11, 24; Acts 20:29, 30, 31; 2 Thessalonians 2:11; 1 Timothy 4:1 and following; 2 Timothy 3:5, 6 & 4:3, 4; 2 Peter 2:1, 2.* Concerning their signs and miracles, *Matthew 24:24; 2 Thessalonians 2:9; Revelation 16:14.* They are called Antichrists, *1 John 2:18, 22.* Feigning angelic religion, *Colossians 2:18.* Full of superstition, *in the same place, verse 23 & 2 Corinthians 2:17.* Enemies of the cross of Christ, and caring for earthly things, *Philippians 3:18, 19.* Whose God is their belly, *in the same place.* Whom they serve, *Romans 16:18.* Deceitful workers, *2 Corinthians 11:13.* Perverting the Gospel, *Galatians 1:7.* Making a trade of the word of God, *2 Corinthians 2:17.* And corrupting it, *2 Corinthians 11:3, 4.* Preaching fables, *2 Timothy 4:4.* Teaching the commands of men, *Colossians 2:8, 23.* They are called thieves and murderers, *John 10:8.* And savage wolves, *Acts 20:29; Matthew 7:15.* Sowing demonic doctrine by forbidding marriage and foods, *1 Timothy 4:1, 2, 3.* Wishing to be Teachers though they are unlearned themselves, *1 Timothy 1:7.* Corrupt in understanding and deprived of the truth, *1 Timothy 6:5.* Thinking that godliness is a means of gain, *in the same place.* A description of these men, *1 Timothy 1:4; 1 and following & 6:3 and following; 2 Timothy 3:2 and following & 4:3, 4; 2 Peter 2:12 and following; Jude 8 and following; Revelation 16:2, 9, 10, 11 & 17:3 and following & 18:16.* They are known by their fruits, *Matthew 7:16.*

**Foreskin** <note>original: "Prapucium"</note>. Thus they called the part which was cut from the bodies of boys among the Jews. Hence, by this name were signified the <term>uncircumcised</term> <note>original Greek: ἀπερίτμητοι</term> gentiles, *Acts 11:3; Romans 2:25, 26 & 4:10, 11 & 4:25, 26; 1 Corinthians 7:18, 19; Galatians 2:7 & 5:6 & 6:15; Ephesians 2:11; Colossians 2:13 & 3:11.*

**Presbyter**, a name of Greek origin, signifies an elder; and by the usage of both Jewish and Ecclesiastical speech, it signifies a presiding officer and a leader, *Matthew 16:21 & 26:3; Mark 7:1, 5 & 14:43; Acts 4:5 & 6:12; 1 Timothy 5:1; Titus 1:5.*

**Praetorium** <note>The headquarters of a Roman governor</note>, the Greeks retained this Latin name. It is properly the tent of a praetor, and signifies the place designated for the judgments and administration of the Romans, which to the Greeks is an <term>inner court</term> <note>original Greek: αὐλή</term>, *Matthew 27:27; Mark 15:16; John 18:28 & 19:9; Acts 23:35.*

**Firstfruits**, offerings of the first fruits, or the first parts of the fruits offered. From this the name is transferred to mean the <term>firstfruits</term> <note>original Greek: ἀπαρχὰς</note> of the Spirit, *Romans 8:23.* As if consecrated, *1 Corinthians 15:20, 23 & 16:15; 2 Thessalonians 2:13; Revelation 14:4.*

**Firstborn**, Jesus Christ the son of the virgin Mary, *Matthew 1, 25.* The firstborn among many brothers, *Romans 8:29.* Before all creation, *Colossians 1:15.* From death, *1 Corinthians 15:20; Colossians 1:18; Revelation 1:5.*

**Prince** <note>meaning a chief or ruler</note>. Christ is the Prince of shepherds, *1 Peter 5:4.* And the head of all principality, *Colossians 2:10.* The princes of the nations exercise lordship, *Mark 10:42.* The prince of the world, whom Christ conquered, *John 12:31 & 14:30 & 16:11.* Whom the Apostle Paul calls the prince of the power of the air, *Ephesians 2:2.*

**To Prove** <note>or "to test"</note>. The spirits, *1 John 4:1.* Oneself, *1 Corinthians 11:28; 2 Corinthians 13:5.* All things, *1 Thessalonians 5:21.*

**Proconsul**, one who governed a consular province in place of a Consul, *Acts 13:12 & 18:12 & 19:38; James 1:22.*

**Promises** pertaining to the gentiles, *Acts 2:39; Romans 4:16; Galatians 3:28, 29; 2 Corinthians 7:1.*

**Prophet**, a Greek name, signifies a seer; the Greeks also called them <term>divinely inspired</term> <note>original Greek: θεοφόρους</note>, as if they were interpreters of divine things, explaining the will and judgment of God. In Ecclesiastical speech, Prophets are those adorned with a singular gift of predicting the future and declaring secrets, *Matthew 2:15, 17 & 10:41 & 11:9 & 21:11; Mark 6:4; Luke 1:76 & 4:17; John 1:21, 23; 1 Corinthians 14:1, 3 and following; Titus 1:12.* False prophets, *Acts 20:29.*

**Proselytes**, a Greek name, those who are <term>newcomers</term> <note>original Greek: προσήλυθοι</term>, strangers; properly said of those who had recently joined the Jews as observers of their religion, *Matthew 23:15; Acts 2:10.*

**Neighbor**, is every other person in the human race, *Luke 10:30.* To be loved, *Matthew 22:39.* Thus the Law is fulfilled, *Romans 13:10.*

**Psalms**, hymns, Greek names for musical harmonies, *1 Corinthians 14:15; Ephesians 5:19.*

**Publicans**, the name of an order of people who held the tax farming of the Roman people in the provinces. The Jews hated their company most intensely, both because of the burden of their exactions and because of their hatred for the Roman Empire, *Matthew 18:17 & 21:31, 32; Luke 5:29, 39 & 7:34 & 15:1 & 18:10 and following.*

**Punishment**, that is, the notice and correction of manifest crimes,

<column-break/>

committed to magistrates, *Romans 13:4; 1 Peter 2:14.* Punishment of the faithful by chastising, *1 Corinthians 5:1, 5 & 11:32; 1 Peter 4:12.* Eternal punishment awaits the unfaithful, *Matthew 3:10 & 25:46; Mark 9:43; 2 Thessalonians 2:19; Revelation 20:10, 15 & 21:8 & 22:15.*

**Purgatory**, specifically the fire, which is <term>purifying fire</term> <note>original Greek: πῦρ καθαρτήριον</note>; Scripture is ignorant of this name <note>The author is noting that the word "Purgatory" does not appear in the Bible</note>. There is, however, one purgation or purification, a washing from sins, which we have from Christ and through Christ, *Matthew 1:21 & 25:28; Mark 2:10 & 14:24; Luke 1:31 & 22:20; John 1:29 & 3:16; Acts 5:31; Ephesians 1:7; Hebrews 1:3 & 9:14; 1 Peter 3:18; 1 John 2:2; Revelation 1:5.* See the word **Christ** as the victim.

**Purple and Scarlet**, precious dyes for clothes, which are then called purple and scarlet. **Byssus** is the name for the material, that is, excellent linen, from which come "fine linens," *Luke 16:19; Revelation 17:4 & 18:12.*

->### Q.<-

**Quadrans**, three ounces, which is the fourth part of an *as* <note>a small Roman coin</note>, *Matthew 5:26; Mark 12:42.*

->### R.<-

**Rabbi**, a Hebrew word, signifying master and teacher, *John 1:38.* This title is not to be sought after, *Matthew 23:7.*

**Raca**, a Hebrew word, an indication of an indignant and moved soul, which to the Greeks are <term>exclamations of complaint</term> <note>original Greek: σχετλιαστικὰ ἐπιῤῥήματα</note>, and to the Latins, Interjections, *Matthew 5:22.*

**Account** <note>original: "Ratio"</note>. To settle accounts, or to compare and render them, *Matthew 18:24; Luke 16:2.* An account must be given, that is, a defense must be spoken, for every idle word, *Matthew 12:36.* An account of faith must be given, *1 Peter 3:15.* The example of the Apostle Paul, *Acts 26:2 and following.* Concerning all things that each person has done, *Romans 14:12.*

**Reconciliation** with God, see the word **Christ**. With a neighbor, *Matthew 5:24, 25.*

**Redemption**, Liberation, by the payment of a price. Our redemption through Christ, see the word **Christ**. This was ordained before the foundation of the world, *1 Peter 1:20; Revelation 5:9, 10.* Redeemed from the curse of the Law, *Galatians 3:13 & 4:5.* Sealed for the day of redemption, *Ephesians 4:30.*

**Kingdom of Christ**, *Matthew 13:11, 41; Luke 1:33 & 22:29; 1 Corinthians 15:24; Colossians 1:13; 2 Peter 1:11.* Kingdom of heaven and of God, *John 3:5.* The heirs of this are not the wicked and shameful, *1 Corinthians 6:9; Galatians 5:19 and following.* Flesh and blood do not possess this, *1 Corinthians 15:50.* Some are made eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of God, *Matthew 19:12.* The kingdom of God is not food and drink, *Romans 14:17.* But righteousness and peace, joy in the Holy Spirit, *in the same place.* It is not in words, *1 Corinthians 4:20.* It is within us, *Luke 17:21.* Its salvation is unto eternal life, *2 Timothy 4:18.* One must enter this through tribulations, *Acts 14:22.* Those worthy of this, *1 Thessalonians 2:12; 2 Thessalonians 1:15.*

**Rule**, <term>canon</term> <note>original Greek: κανὼν</note>, that which is right and true, *2 Corinthians 10:13; Philippians 3:16; Galatians 6:16.*

**Religion**, true, *James 1:27.* False and superstitious, *Luke 11:39, 40; Colossians 2:8, 16.*

**Remission of sins**, or free dismissal, *Romans 4:6.* Through Christ alone, *Acts 5:31 & 10:13; Ephesians 1:7.* See the word **Christ**. Favor to be given and others to be forgiven, *Matthew 5:24 & 18:21, 22; Mark 11:25; Luke 15:22 & 17:4; Ephesians 4:2; James 5:19.*

**Reprobate**, that which is cast away and rejected in extreme perversity, *Matthew 7:22 & 8:12 & 13:42 & 21:42; Luke 3:7; John 3:18 & 5:29 & 9:31 & 10:26 & 12:39, 40; Romans 1, 24 and following & 9:33 & 11:1 and following; 2 Corinthians 3:12 and following; 2 Thessalonians 2:8, 9; Titus 3:10, 11; Hebrews 10:26 and following; Revelation 17:1.*

**Divorce** <note>original: "Repudium"</note>, a bill of divorce, *Matthew 5:31 & 19:7.*

**Rest**, *Matthew 11:29; 1 Thessalonians 1:7; Hebrews 4:1; Revelation 4:8.*

**Resurrection**, is a return into life with a living body, *Matthew 25:32; Luke 2:34; John 5:25 & 6:39 & 11:23, 24; Acts 17:31 & 24:15, 21; 1 Corinthians 15:4, 12 and following; 2 Corinthians 5:15.* The excellent resurrection of Christ, *Matthew 28:6, 7; Mark 16:6, 9; Luke 24:6; John 20:9; 1 Corinthians 15:4; Colossians 1:18.* The efficacy of this, *Romans 4:25 & 6:10; 1 Peter 1:3.*

**God the King**, *1 Timothy 1:17.* The faithful are kings of Christ, *1 Peter 2:9; Revelation 1:6 & 5:10.*

**Wrinkle**, <term>rhytis</term> <note>original Greek: ῥυτίς</note>, a deformity, such as belongs to aging bodies, *Ephesians 5:27.*

->### S.<-

**Sabbath**, a Hebrew word, which the Evangelists retained in their writings. It has the meaning of rest and holidays, in which one would cease from doing work. However, the Jews were commanded to keep the seventh day: which if it fell at the time of other holidays, it was considered even more of a feast, *John 19.*

**Priest and high priest**, this is the only-begotten Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, *Hebrews 5:5, 6, and 7:21 & following, and 8:1, and 9:8 & following.* In him, the faithful of Christ are also priests themselves, *1 Peter 2:9; Revelation 1:6.* Offering a living sacrifice, *Romans 12:1, 2; 1 Peter 2:5; Hebrews 13:15.*

**Sacrament**, a hidden matter not perceived by the senses, a sacred thing from which the uninitiated are kept away <note>original: "profani", meaning those "outside the temple" or the unholy</note>, *1 Corinthians 4:1; Ephesians 1:9, and 3:3, and 5:32; Colossians 1:26; 1 Timothy 3:16; Revelation 1:20, and 17:5, 7.*

**Salvation**, the preservation of life through the grace of Christ, *Titus 3:5.* The end of our faith, *1 Peter 1:9.* See the word "Christ." **Salvation of the nations**, *Romans 11:12.* Near at hand, *Romans 13:11.* **Helmet of salvation**, *Ephesians 6:17; 1 Thessalonians 5:8.* **To work out salvation**, *Philippians 2:12.*

**Holy**, carries the meaning of that which is pure and polluted or stained by no blemish or spot; it refers to the holy place, and the holy Angels and men. But God is holy in an exceptional manner, and this is the peculiar title of the Holy Spirit. The pious and faithful are called "holy" <note>often translated as "Saints"</note>, washed from the filth of this world, *Romans 1:2, and 8:9, and 16:16; 1 Corinthians 1:2; 2 Corinthians 1:2; Ephesians 1:4; Philippians 1:1, and 4:21, 22; Philemon 5; Hebrews 3:1; 1 Peter 1:3, 15.* That which is holy is not to be given to dogs, *Matthew 7:6.*

**Blood**, the condition, nature, and life of humans, *John 1:13; Hebrews 12:4.* And it signifies the same in *Matthew 23:35, and 27:4, 24.* The Blood of Christ, *Matthew 26:28; Luke 22:20; John 6:53; 1 Corinthians 10:16, and 11:25; Ephesians 1:7; Colossians 1:14; Hebrews 9:14, and 10:19, and 12:14, and 13:21; 1 Peter 1:19; 1 John 1:7; Revelation 1:5.*

**Wisdom of God**, see the words "Christ" and "Gospel." **Wisdom of the world**, *Romans 8:7; 1 Corinthians 2:3, 20, and 2:4, 5, 6, and 3:19.* **Devilish wisdom**, *James 3:15.*

**Satan**, a Hebrew word, <note>Greek: ὁ Σατανᾶς</note> "the Adversary," an impure spirit, the adversary of God, and the enemy of the human race, *Matthew 4:10, and 12:26; Luke 22:3; 1 Corinthians 7:5; 2 Corinthians 2:11; 1 Thessalonians 2:18; 2 Thessalonians 2:9; Revelation 20:2.* He enters into Judas, *John 13:29.* The Apostle Paul delivers a fornicator to Satan, *1 Corinthians 5:5.* He transforms himself into an Angel of light, *2 Corinthians 11:14.* An angel of Satan striking the Apostle Paul, *2 Corinthians 12:7.* The Apostle Peter is called Satan, *Matthew 16:23; Mark 8:33.*

**Offense** <note>original: "Scandalum", also meaning a stumbling block</note>, a name of Greek origin, signifying an impediment and a cause of tripping, by which someone who is entangled falls, that is, ruin: and the verb, from the Greek, **to cause to stumble** <note>original: "Scandalizo"</note>, *Matthew 11:6, and 13:57, and 18:7, 8, 9, and 24:19, and 26:31, 33; Mark 4:17, and 6:3, and 9:42, 43, and 14:27, 29; Luke 2:34, and 7:23, and 17:1, 2; John 6:61, and 16:1,; Romans 9:33, and 11:9, and 14:13; 1 Corinthians 1:23, and 8:13; 2 Corinthians 11:29; Galatians 5:11; 1 Peter 2:8.* **Offense to be avoided**, *Matthew 17:27, and 18:6 & following; Mark 9:42 & following; Luke 17:1, 2; Romans 14:21.* Not to be cared for <note>i.e., when the offense is taken by the self-righteous</note>, *Matthew 15:12, 13; Galatians 2:14, 15.*

**Sexual immorality forbidden**, *Acts 15:29; Romans 1:29; Galatians 5:19, 21; Ephesians 5:3; 1 Corinthians 5:1, and 6:9, and 7:2, and 10:8; 2 Corinthians 12:21; Colossians 3:5, 6; 1 Thessalonians 4:3; 1 Timothy 1:9, 10; Hebrews 12:16, and 13:4; 1 Peter 2:11; Jude 7.* **It signifies idolatry**, *Revelation 2:21, 22, and 14:4, and 17:2, 5, and 18:3.*

**Scribes**, those professing knowledge of the Holy Scripture, *Matthew 2:4, and 5:21, and 8:19, and 13:52, and 15:1, and 21:15, and 23:23, 25, 27.*

**Sense** <note>Latin: "Sensus", referring to the mind or faculty of understanding</note>, <note>Greek: νοῦς</note> "mind," opinion, and intelligence, *Romans 1:28, and 11:34, and 12:2, and 14:5; 1 Corinthians 1:10, and 2:16; Philippians 4:7; Ephesians 4:17.* <note>Greek: φρόνημα</note> "way of thinking," *1 Corinthians 14:20.* <note>Greek: διάνοια</note> "intellect," *2 Corinthians 11:3.* <note>Greek: αἰσθητήριον</note> "organ of sense," *Philippians 1:9.* <note>Greek: διάνοια</note> "understanding," *Hebrews 5:14.* <note>Greek: διάνοια</note> "mind," *Colossians 1:21.*

**Stadium**, a certain distance, from the Greek word: **a Stadium has 600 feet**, *Luke 24:13; John 6:19, and 11:18; 1 Corinthians 9:24; Revelation 14:20, and 21:16.*

**Stater**, a Greek name; it was a <note>Greek: στατήρ</note> "stater," that is, it was valued at four denarii, *Matthew 17:27.*

**The Proud and arrogant**, *Luke 1:51; Romans 1:30, and 12:16; 1 Corinthians 4:7, and 8:1; 2 Corinthians 11:18 and 12:20; Galatians 5:25, 26, and 6:3; Colossians 2:18; Ephesians 2:9; Philippians 2:3; 1 Timothy 3:6, and 6:20; 2 Timothy 3:4; Titus 1:7; James 4:13; 1 Peter 5:5; Jude 16; Revelation 17:23 & following, and 18:7.*

# T.

**Tabernacle**, an allegory of the two tabernacles, *Hebrews 9:1 & following.* <note>Greek: παρασκευή</note> "preparation," a living body, *2 Corinthians 5:4; 2 Peter 1:13.*

**Talent**, a Greek name for a certain weight and sum of money. It had six hundred Minas, and each individual Mina had one hundred drachmas; and it is established that a drachma is a denarius, from which the rest may be easily calculated, *Matthew 18:24, and 25:15; Revelation 16:21.*

**Spiritual Temple**, *1 Corinthians 3:17; 2 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 2:22; Revelation 21:22.* **The Temple of Jerusalem**, *Matthew 4:5, and 21:12, and 24:1; Mark 11:11; Luke 19:1, and 24:53; John 2:14.* **Merchants cast out of the temple**, *Matthew 21:12; Mark 11:11; Luke 19:45; John 2:15.* **God does not dwell in temples made by hands**, *Acts 7:48, and 17:24.* **Temple metaphorically, the body**, *John 2:19; 1 Corinthians 3:16, and 6:19; 2 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 2:21.*

**Time**. The moments of future time are not known by men, *Acts 1:7.* **The time of Christ's coming is defined**, *Mark 1, 15; Romans 5:6 & following; 2 Corinthians 6:2; Galatians 4:4.* **Where also is the fullness of time**. **Our time is short**, *1 Corinthians 7:29.* **The opportunity of time is to be redeemed** <note>meaning to make the most of it</note>, *Ephesians 5:16; Colossians 4:4.*

**Darkness**, *Matthew 27:45; John 20:1.* Metaphorically, sin and ignorance of the truth, *Matthew 6:23; John 1:5, and 12:35; Romans 13:12; Ephesians 5:2; 1 Thessalonians 5:4, 5; 1 John 1:6, 7, and 2:8 & following.*

**Temptation**, of the Holy ones <note>original: "Sanctorum"</note>, *Hebrews 11:17; James 1:12; 1 Peter 1:6.* **The treacherous and destructive temptation of the Devil**, *Matthew 4:1; Luke 4:1; Acts 5:3; 1 Corinthians 7:5; Galatians 6:1; 1 Thessalonians 3:5; 1 Timothy 6:9; Revelation 2:10.* **God delivers from temptation**, *Matthew 6:13; 1 Corinthians 10:13; Hebrews 2:18; 2 Peter 2:9; Revelation 3:10.* **This must be prayed for**, *Matthew 6:13, and 26:41; Luke 11:4, and 21:40, 46.* **God is not to be tempted**, *Matthew 4:7; Acts 5:9, and 15:10; 1 Corinthians 10:9; Hebrews 3:9.*

# INDEX OF WORDS AND PLACES.
<meta>Catchword: LIFE</meta>

**Testament**, <note>original Greek: diathēkē</note>, has the meaning of a covenant and a confirmation of things that ought to be done and kept. Chief among these are the decrees of what is properly called a testament—that is, the legal declaration or witnessing of one's last will. This is the will of the Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, toward the human race, ratified by his own death, *Matthew 26:28; 1 Corinthians 11:25; Galatians 4:24; Hebrews 8:8, 9:15, 10:29, 12:24, and 13:20.* The **Old Testament** or covenant, *Acts 3:25; Romans 6:14, 15, 8:15, and 9:9 & following; 2 Corinthians 3:14; Galatians 4:24, 25.*

**Testimony** <note>or Witness</note>, of two or three, *John 8:17; 2 Corinthians 13:1; Hebrews 10:28.* Testimony of the Spirit, *John 15:26; Acts 5:32; Romans 8:16; 1 John 5:6.* Of conscience, *Romans 2:15 and 9:1; 2 Corinthians 1, 12.* Of Scripture, *John 5:14.* Testimony toward others, *Acts 6:3; 1 Timothy 3:7 and 5:10.* Of works, *John 10:37, 38.* To give testimony to the truth, *John 1:7, 8, 34 and 18:37; Acts 4:33; 1 Corinthians 15:15; 1 Timothy 6:12, 13; 2 Timothy 1:8; Revelation 1:2.* **False Testimony**, *Matthew 19:18 and 26:59; Mark 10:19; Acts 6:13.*

**Treasure**, in heaven; *Matthew 6:20.* All divine treasures are in Christ, *Colossians 2:3.* Fleeting treasure, *Luke 12:22; James 5:1, 2 & following.* This name is Greek but common among the Latins. Here it is also called by the foreign name *Gaza* <note>a Persian word for treasure</note>, from which comes *Gazophylacium* <note>Treasury</note>, where the "Gaza" was kept—referring to stored public wealth, much like we would call a treasury.

**Fear**, of God as if from sons <note>filial fear rather than terror</note>, *Matthew 10:31; Luke 1:74; Acts 9:31 and 10:2; 2 Corinthians 5:11; Ephesians 5:21; 1 Peter 2:16.* **Slavish fear**, *Romans 8:15; 1 John 4:18; Revelation 21:7.* Fear owed to men, *Romans 13:7; 2 Corinthians 7:11; Ephesians 6:5; Colossians 3:18, 22; 1 Peter 2:18.* Forbidden fear, *Matthew 10:26, 28, 31; Luke 12:4; 1 Peter 3:14.* Worldly fear, *John 9:22 and 12:42.* It is also a disturbance of one's favor or standing, *Matthew 27:54 and 28:4, 5; Luke 1:12, 2:9, and 22:2; Acts 2:43 and 5:5, 11; 2 Corinthians 7:5; Revelation 11:11.*

**Traitor** and **Betrayal**, that is, one who hands over and the act of handing over, *Matthew 26:21, 23, 24; Mark 14:18, 21; Luke 9:44; Acts 7:52; 2 Timothy 3:4.*

**Tribulation** is affliction. Of spouses, *1 Corinthians 7:32 & following.* Of those who love God, *Acts 7:6, 7 and 14:21; Hebrews 10:33, 34 and 11:36, 37; Revelation 1:9.* To be borne patiently and confidently, *Romans 12:12; 1 Thessalonians 3:4, 7.* To be boasted of, *Romans 5:3; 2 Thessalonians 1:11, 12.* To be rejoiced in, *2 Corinthians 7:4 and 8:2; 1 Thessalonians 1:6 and 3:9; Hebrews 10:34.* The afflicted are to be comforted, *2 Corinthians 1:4, 5.* This pertains to **Testing**, *1 Peter 4:12; Revelation 2:10.* To **Correction**, *Hebrews 12:6.* One should pray for it to be turned away, *Mark 13:18, 19 & following.*

**Tribute** and tax, *Matthew 17:25 and 22:17; Luke 20:22; Romans 13:7.*

**Sadness**, healthy, *Matthew 26:38; 2 Corinthians 6:10.* Destructive, *Matthew 26:22; Luke 18:23.*

**Tyranny** and cruelty, *Matthew 2, 16 and 4:9, 10; Acts 7:57, 58 and 12:2, 3; 1 Timothy 3:2 & following.*

->V.<-

**Vessel**, *Romans 9:21.* It also denotes every tool or instrument of a house, *Acts 10:11; 2 Timothy 2:20, 21.* <note>Greek: skeuos</note>, *1 Thessalonians 4:4.*

**Pardon**, see the term **Remission**.

**Word**, is whatever is pronounced by the mouth, and by Hebrew custom also the very thing that is indicated by words, <note>Greek: rhēma</note>, *Luke 1:4.* But in an exalted sense, <note>Greek: logos</note>, regarding the Son of God, *John 1:1; Hebrews 11:3; Revelation 19:13.* The **Word of God** is Spirit and life, *John 6:63.* It is Truth, *John 17:17.* It is the Power of God, *1 Corinthians 1:18.* The Sword of the Spirit, *Ephesians 6:17.* Two-edged, *Revelation 1:16 and 19:15.* The Word of eternal life, *Matthew 4:4; Luke 4:4; John 6:68; Acts 5:20; Philippians 2:16.* The Word of truth, *2 Corinthians 6:7; Ephesians 1:13; James 1:18.* Of grace, *Luke 4:22.* Of salvation, *Acts 13:26.* Of reconciliation, *2 Corinthians 5:19.* Of the cross, *1 Corinthians 1:18.* Foolishness to those who are perishing, *ibid.* Living and effective, *Hebrews 4:12.* Illuminating hearts, *1 Peter 1:13.* Remaining forever, *Matthew 24:35; Mark 13:31; Luke 21:33; 1 Peter 1:23.* The power of saving souls, *James 1:21.* Working in those who believe, *1 Thessalonians 2:13.* Dwelling in the faithful of Christ, *1 John 2:14; Colossians 3:26.* Sanctifying all things, *1 Timothy 4:4, 5.* Growing and bearing fruit, *Acts 6:7, 12:24, 13:49, and 19:20; Colossians 1:6; 1 Thessalonians 1:4, 8; 2 Thessalonians 3:1.* Seed, used **parabolically**, *Matthew 13:19; Mark 4:14; Luke 8:11.* To be preached to all, *Matthew 28:19; Mark 16:15; Acts 1:8.* Not to be thrown before those who despise it, *Matthew 7:6.* To be kept, *Matthew 7:24; John 14:23; James 1:21, 22; 2 Peter 3:17.* The profit of those who corrupt this through trade <note>mercenary preaching</note>, *2 Corinthians 2:17 and 4:2; 1 Timothy 6:5.*

**Truth** is Christ, *John 14:6.* Of the Holy Spirit, *John 16:13; 1 John 5:6.* Of the Gospel, *John 17:17; 2 Timothy 2:15; 2 Peter 1:16, 17; James 1:18.* To follow the truth, *Ephesians 4:15, 25 and 6:14; 1 Timothy 3:15; 1 John 3:18; 2 John 1:2, and 3:4.* Nothing is valid against this, *2 Corinthians 13:8.* Those turning away from the truth, *Galatians 3:1 and 5:7; 2 Timothy 4:4; Titus 1:14; Hebrews 6:4 and 10:26; 2 Peter 2:2.* Those resisting the truth, *Romans 2:8; Galatians 3:7; 2 Timothy 2:25 and 3:8.*

**Clothing**, we ought not to be anxious about this, *Matthew 6:28.* Against excessive clothing, *Luke 3:11 and 7:25.* That it should be simple and honest, *1 Timothy 2:9; 1 Peter 3:3, 4.* **Spiritual clothing**, *Matthew 22:12; Luke 24:4; Romans 13:12; 2 Corinthians 5:3; Galatians 3:27; Ephesians 4:24.*

**Way**, Christ is the way to the Father, *John 14:16.* The just way of God, *Romans 11:33; Revelation 15:3.* It signifies a sect or profession, *Acts 9:2.* Method and guidance, *Acts 2:28, 18:25, and 19:9.*

**Sustenance**, things necessary for leading a life. Sustenance and covering <note>food and clothing</note>, *1 Timothy 6:8.* This is spiritual food, *John 4:34 and 6:27 & following.* Of the body, *Hebrews 12:16 and 13:9.* The distinction between foods removed by God, *Matthew 15:17 & following; Mark 7:18 & following; Luke 10:7, 8; Acts 10:14, 15 and 11:9; Romans 14:14, 15; 1 Corinthians 6:13, 8:9, and 10:25 & following; Colossians 2:16; 1 Timothy 4:3, 4; Luke 20:47.*

**Widow**, widows are commended, *1 Timothy 5:3 & following.* Concerning them, *1 Corinthians 7:39, 40.* Devourers of widows, *Matthew 23:14; Mark 12:40; Luke 20:47.*

**To Watch and be attentive**, *Matthew 24:42, 25:13, and 26:41; Mark 14:34, 38, and Luke 12:37, 40; Romans 13:11; 1 Corinthians 15:34 and 16:13; 2 Corinthians 6:5; Ephesians 5:13; 1 Thessalonians 5:6; 1 Peter 4:7; Revelation 3:2 and 16:15.*

**Watches**, *2 Corinthians 11:27.* These are the divided times of the night guard, *Matthew 14:25; Luke 2:8 and 12:38.*

**Vengeance** belongs to God, *Romans 12:19; 1 Thessalonians 5:15; 1 Peter 3:9.* Vengeance upon the ungodly, *Luke 18:7; 2 Thessalonians 4:8; Hebrews 10:30, 31; Revelation 6:10 and 19:2.*

**Vineyard**, the parable of the vineyard, *Matthew 12:1 & following; Mark 12:1; Luke 20:9.* Christ is the true vine, *John 15:1.*

**Wine**, to be drunk in moderation, *Ephesians 5:18; 1 Timothy 5:23; Titus 2:7. 3.*

**Virginity**, a singular gift of God, *Matthew 19:11; 1 Corinthians 7:7.* Concerning virgins, *ibid.* But chastity is commanded to all.

**Virtue**, <note>Greek: aretē</note>, that which is proper and praiseworthy; <note>Greek: dynamis</note>, the force and efficacy of God working in his own, *1 Corinthians 2:4; Galatians 3:5; Colossians 1:11.* Through the Gospel, *Romans 1, 16; 1 Corinthians 1:18.* Through faith, *1 Peter 1:5.*

**Visitation**, this is inspection. Of orphans and widows, *James 1:27.* Of the sick, *Matthew 25:36; James 5:14.* Of prisoners, *Matthew 25:36; Hebrews 13:3.*

**Life**, of the body, fleeting, *Luke 16:22; Romans 8:20; 1 Corinthians 15:19; Philippians 1:20 & following; James 4:13.* To be disregarded, *Matthew 6:19 and 16:25, 26; Mark 8:34, 35; John 10:11 and 12:25.* **Eternal life**, the knowledge of God and Christ, *John 17:3.* A gift of grace through Christ, *John 3:16, 5:24, 6:27, 40, and 10:28; Romans 6:22; 1 Timothy 1:16 and 6:12; Titus 1:2 and 3:7; 1 John 2:25 and 5:11; Revelation 22:17.* **Way of life**, of Elders and Spouses, see those terms; of Elders and faithful Spouses, *Titus 2:2; 1 Peter 3:1, 7 and 5:1 & following;* see the term **Faithful**. Forbidden habits of life, *1 Corinthians 5:9 & following; 2 Corinthians 6:14; Ephesians 4:17 and 5:13 & following; 1 Peter 1:14.*

**Union** and being **Of One Mind**, *Acts 1:14, 2:1, 4:24, 32, and 5:13; Romans 12:16 and 15:5, 6; 1 Corinthians 1, 10 and 12:17; Ephesians 4:3; Philippians 1:27, 2:2, 3:16, and 8:8.* One in God, *John 17:21.* In Christ, *Galatians 3:28.*

**Calling** <note>or Vocation</note> through Christ, *Matthew 8:22 and 9:9; John 6:37, 13:20, and 15:16; 1 Thessalonians 3:7.* Of God, *Romans 11:29; 1 Peter 5:10.* To salvation and eternal life, *Matthew 20:16; John 10:28, 29; Romans 1:6, 8:30, and 9:11; 1 Corinthians 1:9; Galatians 1:6; 1 Thessalonians 2:12; 1 Timothy 6:12; 2 Timothy 1:9, 15; Hebrews 9:15; 1 Peter 3:9; 2 Peter 1:3, 10; Jude 1.* Of the Gentiles, *John 10:16; Romans 9:24 and 11:17 & following, and 15:16 & following.* To the preaching of the Gospel, *Matthew 4:16, 17; Mark 3:8; Luke 6:17; Romans 1:16 and 10:12, 20; 1 Corinthians 1:24; Galatians 2:16; 1 Timothy 2:7.* Diverse callings, *1 Corinthians 12:5 & following.* Each person's own calling, which is each person's own state of life, *1 Corinthians 7:20.*

**Will**, of God, the cause of all things, *Ephesians 1:11; 1 Thessalonians 4:14; Hebrews 2:10; 1 Peter 2:15; Revelation 4:12.* To be prayed that it be done, *Matthew 6:10 and 26:42; John 4:34; Colossians 1:9; Hebrews 13:21.* All things are to be committed to this, *Matthew 10:30; Romans 15:1; 1 Corinthians 4:5 and 16:7; 1 Peter 4:2 and 5:7; James 4:15.* **Human will** without God is the cause of no good thing, *Matthew 10:20, 39, 11:17 & following, 13:4, 5 & following, 16:17, and 23:4 & following; Luke 24:5, 21, 25; John 1:5, 11, 13, 3:5, 6, 6:7, 28, 63, 8:37, 47, 14:5, 17, 15:5, 17:14, 25, and 19:8 & following; Acts 6:2, 3; Romans 7:18 and 8:7, 8, and 9:16; 1 Corinthians 1:21, 2:14, 3:7, 4:7, and 15:10; Galatians 1:15, 16 and 5:17; Ephesians 1:12; Philippians 2:13; 1 Peter 1:3; 1 John 2:29; James 1:17.*

**Pleasure** to be fled from, *Luke 8:14; Titus 2:12 and 3:3; 1 Peter 4:2, 3.* **Pleasure-seekers**, *Luke 15:13; Ephesians 5:3, 4, 18; 1 Timothy 5:6; 2 Timothy 3:4; 2 Peter 2:10, 13; James 5:5; Revelation 18:3, 22, 23.*

**Vows**, a religious promise, *Acts 18:18.* Wicked vows, *Acts 23:12.*

**Voice** of Christ is heard by his own sheep, *John 10:16.* Emptiness of voices <note>empty talk</note> to be avoided, *1 Timothy 6:20.*

**Usury** prohibited, *Luke 6:35.*

# THE LIFE OF SAINT MATTHEW
## BY SAINT JEROME.

MATTHEW, who is also called Levi, and who went from being a tax collector <note>original: "publicano"</note> to an Apostle, was the first in Judea to compose the Gospel of Christ in Hebrew letters and words for the sake of those from the circumcision <note>meaning Jewish converts to Christianity</note> who had believed. It is not sufficiently certain who later translated it into Greek. Furthermore, the Hebrew text itself is preserved to this day in the library at Caesarea, which Pamphilus the martyr <note>a 3rd-century scholar and bishop who assembled a famous library</note> most diligently assembled. I also had the opportunity to transcribe it from the Nazarenes <note>an early group of Jewish Christians</note> who use this volume in the city of Beroea in Syria. In this work, it should be noted that whenever the Evangelist makes use of testimonies from the Old Testament—whether speaking in his own voice or in the person of our Lord and Savior—he does not follow the authority of the Seventy Translators <note>the Septuagint, the standard Greek translation of the Old Testament</note>, but the Hebrew original. Two examples of this are: *Out of Egypt I have called my son* <note>Matthew 2:15</note>, and, *For he shall be called a Nazarene* <note>Matthew 2:23</note>.

# THE LIFE OF SAINT MARK
## BY SAINT JEROME.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'M' containing a miniature illustration of a scholar or saint (St. Mark) seated at a desk writing, surrounded by ornamental floral and scroll patterns.</image-desc>

MARK, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, wrote a short Gospel at the request of the brothers in Rome, based on what he had heard Peter relating. When Peter had heard it, he approved it and published it by his own authority to be read in the Church, just as Clement writes in the sixth book of his *Outlines* <note>original: "Hypotyposeon," a lost work of Clement of Alexandria</note>. Papias, the Bishop of Hierapolis, also makes mention of this Mark, as does Peter in his first Epistle, figuratively signifying Rome under the name of Babylon: *She who is in Babylon, elect together with you, greets you, and so does Mark my son.* <note>1 Peter 5:13</note> Having taken up the Gospel which he himself had composed, he set out for Egypt; and as the first to preach Christ at Alexandria, he established a Church of such great doctrine and restraint <note>original: "continentiae," referring to self-discipline or asceticism</note> in life that he compelled all followers of Christ to follow his example. Finally, Philo <note>a prominent Jewish philosopher from Alexandria</note>, the most eloquent of the Jews, seeing the first Church at Alexandria still following Jewish customs <note>original: "Judaizantem"</note>, wrote a book about their way of life as if in praise of his own nation. And just as Luke narrates that the believers in Jerusalem held all things in common, so Philo recorded for memory what he saw being done in Alexandria under Mark’s teaching. He died in the eighth year of Nero and was buried at Alexandria, with Anianus succeeding him.

# THE LIFE OF SAINT LUKE
## BY SAINT JEROME.

<image-desc>Decorative historiated initial 'L' depicting a bearded figure, likely Saint Luke the Evangelist, seated at a desk and writing in a book. An ox, his traditional iconographic symbol, is visible in the background.</image-desc>

LUKE, a physician of Antioch, as his writings indicate, was not ignorant of the Greek language. He was a follower of the Apostle Paul and the companion of all his travels. He wrote a Gospel, of which the same Paul says: 
> *“We have sent,”* he said, *“with him the brother whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the Churches.”* 

And to the Colossians: 
> *“Luke, the most dear physician, greets you.”* 

And to Timothy: 
> *“Luke alone is with me.”* 

He also published another distinguished volume, which is pre-titled the <term>Acts of the Apostles</term> <note>original Greek: Πράξεις Ἀποστόλων (Praxeis Apostolon)</note>, the history of which reaches until the two-year stay of Paul in Rome—that is, until the fourth year of Nero. From this, we understand that the book was composed in that same city.

<margin>The Travels of Paul and Thecla</margin>
Therefore, the *Travels* <note>original: "Periodus," likely referring to the apocryphal Acts of Paul and Thecla</note> of Paul and Thecla, and the whole story of the baptized Lion, we count among the apocryphal scriptures. For how is it possible that the inseparable companion of the Apostle, among his other deeds, would be ignorant of this alone? But even Tertullian, living near those times, reports that a certain priest in Asia, a <term>devotee</term> <note>original Greek: σπουδαστὴν (spoudastēn), meaning a zealous follower or student</note> of the Apostle Paul, was convicted before John of being the author of the book. He confessed that he had done this out of love for Paul, and for that reason, he was removed from his office <note>original: "excidisse," literally "he fell out," referring to his deposition</note>. Some suspect that whenever Paul says in his Epistles, *“According to my Gospel,”* he is referring to the volume of Luke. And Luke learned the Gospel not only from the Apostle Paul (who had not been with the Lord in the flesh), but from the other Apostles; which he himself also declares at the beginning of his volume, saying: 
> *“Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word.”* 

Therefore, he wrote the Gospel as he had heard it, but he composed the Acts of the Apostles as he had seen it. He lived eighty-four years, having no wife. He was buried at Constantinople, to which city, in the twentieth year of Constantius, his bones were moved from Achaia along with the relics of the Apostle Andrew.

# THE LIFE OF SAINT JOHN

## BY THE DIVINE JEROME <note>Jerome was a 4th-century scholar and theologian best known for translating the Bible into Latin (the Vulgate).</note>

<margin>
John 21.
Matt. 4.
Mark 1.
Luke 5.

1 John 1.
2 John 1.
3 John 1.

JOHN the Apostle, whom Jesus loved most, was the son of Zebedee and the brother of the Apostle James, whom Herod beheaded after the Lord's passion. He was the last of all to write a Gospel, at the request of the Bishops of Asia, to oppose Cerinthus and other heretics—especially the then-rising doctrine of the Ebionites <note>The Ebionites were an early Jewish-Christian sect who emphasized Jewish law and often denied the pre-existence or divinity of Christ.</note>, who assert that Christ did not exist before Mary. Thus, he was compelled to proclaim His divine birth. But they also report another reason for this writing: that when he had read the volumes of Matthew, Mark, and Luke, he approved of the historical text and confirmed they spoke the truth, but noted they had composed the history of only one year—the one in which He suffered—following the imprisonment of John [the Baptist]. Therefore, omitting the year whose deeds had been set forth by the three, he narrated the events of the earlier time, before John was shut in prison, as will be manifest to those who diligently read the four volumes of the Gospels. This also resolves the <term>discrepancy <note>original Greek: διαφωνίαν (diaphonian), meaning a lack of harmony or a contradiction between accounts</note></term> which John appears to have with the others. He also wrote one Epistle, which begins, *That which was from the beginning, which we have heard and seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon and our hands have handled, of the word of life*, which is approved by all churchmen and learned men. The remaining two, which begin, *The Elder to the elect lady and her children*, and the next, *The Elder to the most beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth*, are said to be by John the Presbyter <note>Or "John the Elder"; some early traditions distinguished between John the Apostle and another "Elder John" in Ephesus.</note>, whose second tomb is still shown at Ephesus today. Some believe these are two memorials to the same John the Evangelist; we shall discuss this when we come to Papias, his pupil, in order. In the fourteenth year, therefore, during the second persecution after Nero initiated by Domitian, he was exiled to the island of Patmos, where he wrote the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, which Justin Martyr and Irenaeus interpret. After Domitian was killed and his acts were rescinded by the Senate because of his excessive cruelty, John returned to Ephesus under the Emperor Nerva. Remaining there until the reign of Emperor Trajan, he founded and ruled all the Churches of Asia; worn out by old age, he died in the sixty-eighth year after the Lord's passion and was buried near that same city.

# THE LIFE OF THE HOLY EVANGELIST MATTHEW
## ACCORDING TO SOPHRONIUS <note>Sophronius (c. 560–638 AD) was the Patriarch of Jerusalem and a prolific writer of saintly biographies.</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'M' featuring ornate foliage and geometric patterns.</image-desc>

MATTHEW, also called Levi, an Apostle from the rank of tax collectors <note>original: "τελωνῶν" - publicans or tax gatherers for the Roman Empire</note>, was the first in Judea to compose the Gospel of Christ for those of the circumcision <note>That is, Jewish believers.</note> who had believed. He composed it in Hebrew letters and words; however, it is not known for certain who translated it into Greek. The Hebrew version itself is preserved to this day in the library at Caesarea, which was diligently established by the martyr Pamphilus. I myself was granted permission to transcribe this volume by the Nazareans <note>An early group of Jewish Christians who maintained Jewish customs.</note> in Beroea, Syria, who make use of it. From this version, one can clearly see that whenever the Evangelist—whether in his own person or the person of our Lord Jesus Christ—makes use of testimonies from the ancient Scriptures, he does not follow the authority of the Seventy translators <note>The Septuagint (LXX), the standard Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note>, but rather the Hebrew text. Two examples of this are: "Out of Egypt I called my son," and "He shall be called a Nazarene."

---

# BY THE MOST GOD-BELOVED ARCHBISHOP OF BULGARIA, LORD THEOPHYLACT <note>Theophylact of Ohrid (c. 1055–1107) was a prominent Byzantine theologian whose commentaries became standard in the Eastern Church.</note>
->Preface to the Gospel according to Matthew.<-

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'O' depicting a seated figure, presumably an evangelist or saint, at a writing desk within a circular medallion, surrounded by a rectangular frame of floral motifs.</image-desc>

NOW THE holy men who lived before the Law <note>Refers to the era before the Ten Commandments were given to Moses.</note> were not taught through writings and books, but having a pure mind, they were enlightened by the radiance of the Spirit, and thus they knew the will of God, for He Himself spoke to them mouth to mouth. Such were Noah, Abraham, Job, and Moses. But when humanity slipped into unworthiness and was no longer fit to be enlightened and taught by the Spirit, the lover of mankind, God, gave the Scriptures, so that through them at least they might be reminded of God's will. In the same way, Christ spoke in person to the Apostles and sent the grace of the Spirit to be their teacher. But because afterward heresies were destined to sprout up and our morals were to be corrupted, He saw fit for the Gospels to be written, so that by being taught the truth from them, we might not be swept away by the falsehood of heresies, nor our morals be completely corrupted. He gave us four Gospels, perhaps because from these we learn the four universal virtues: courage, prudence, justice, and temperance <note>These are the four "cardinal virtues" of classical philosophy, here integrated into Christian teaching.</note>. Courage is found when the Lord says, "Do not fear those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul." Prudence is found when He says, "Be wise as serpents." Justice is taught when He says, "Whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them." And temperance is shown when He declares, "Anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart." In another sense, there are four Gospels because "Gospel" means "Good News," for it announces to us things that are good and fair—namely, the forgiveness of sins, justification, the ascent into heaven, and adoption as children of God. It announces that we received these things easily; for we did not labor to acquire these blessings, nor did we receive them through our own achievements, but by the grace and love of God for mankind were we deemed worthy of such great goods.

**ACCORDING TO MATTHEW.** There are four Evangelists. Of these, two—Matthew and John—were from the choir of the Twelve Apostles, while the other two—Mark and Luke—were from the Seventy <note>Refers to the larger group of disciples mentioned in Luke 10.</note>. Mark was a follower and disciple of Peter, and Luke a follower of Paul. Matthew, then, was the first of all to write the Gospel, in the Hebrew tongue, for those of the Hebrews who had believed, eight years after Christ’s ascension. It is said that John translated this from the Hebrew language into Greek. Mark wrote ten years after the ascension, having been instructed by Peter; Luke wrote after fifteen years; and John, the most profound theologian, after thirty-two years. It is said that after the deaths of the others, the divine Gospels were brought to him while he was still living so that he might examine them and judge if they were written truly. Having seen them and fully accepted them for the sake of the truth, he himself filled in what they had omitted. Those things they spoke of briefly, he expanded upon in his own Gospel; for this reason, he began with "theology" <note>In this context, "theology" refers specifically to the study of Christ's divine nature and pre-existence.</note>. Since the others did not mention the pre-eternal existence of God the Word, he himself spoke theologically about this, so that the Word of God would not be thought to be a mere man—that is, without divinity. For Matthew discusses only the existence of Christ according to the flesh. He wrote for the Hebrews, for whom it was sufficient to learn that Christ was born from Abraham and David; for a believer from the Hebrews is satisfied once he is fully assured that Christ is from David. But you might ask me: "Was one Evangelist not enough?" Listen then: one would have been enough, but that the truth might be shown more clearly, four were written. For when you see these four—who did not meet or sit down together, but were in different places—writing about the same things as if from one mouth, would you not marvel at the truth of the Gospel and say they spoke by the Holy Spirit? And do not tell me that they do not harmonize in everything; for look at the things in which they do not "harmonize": does one say Christ was born and another say He was not? Or one say He rose and another say He did not? God forbid! In the most necessary and essential matters, they harmonize. If, therefore, they did not disagree in the essentials, why do you marvel if they seem to differ in very small details? For this very reason, they are all the more truthful, because they did not harmonize in every single point. For then it might be thought that they wrote by sitting together and consulting one another. But as it is, what this one omitted, that one wrote; and for this reason, they seem to differ in certain things. But let these matters be as they are.

1 *The Gospel according to Matthew*] <note>original: "Evangelium secundum Matthæum"</note> In Greek, "Gospel" means "good news." Although Homer used this word in the *Odyssey* to mean the reward usually given to someone bringing happy news. Therefore, he called it a "Gospel History," rather than a "Prophecy" or anything similar: he marked a new thing with a new term, just as Christ had renewed the terminology for his Apostles.
2 *The book of the generation*] <note>original: "Liber generationis"</note> This is a nominative used absolutely, acting as a title. For Matthew and Mark entered into the Gospel History in the manner of the prophets; indeed, the Prophets are accustomed to begin with a title: "The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz," or "The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah." So too Mark: "The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ." Though I see that Herodotus began his history in a similar fashion: "This is the display of the history of Herodotus of Halicarnassus," <note>original: "Ἡροδότου Ἁλικαρνασσέως ἱστορίης ἀπόδειξις ἥδε"</note> and Lucian in his booklet on Astrology: "The writing concerning the heavens and the stars." <note>original: "Ἀμφὶ τε οὐρανῶν, ἀμφὶ τε τῶν ἀστέρων ἡ γραφή"</note> Thus it appears to have been a custom of the [Greek] nation as well. However, this title does not cover the entire subject matter: for it does not encompass the whole of the Gospel History, but only its beginning and source.
3 *Of the son of David, the son of Abraham*] <note>original: "υἱοῦ Δαβὶδ, υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ"</note> The Greek phrase has some ambiguity: the sense could be "the son of David, which David was the son of Abraham"; or it could be understood that Christ is the son of both. Furthermore, he calls a grandson a "son," just as the Hebrews call "brothers" not only those born of the same parents, but also others propagated from the same family line. It should be noted in passing that Matthew tailored the recital of the genealogy to those for whom he wrote this Gospel. For he wrote to the Hebrews—indeed, it is believed, in Hebrew—whose affections he knew would be most pleased if they saw that Christ was the son of Abraham and David, whose memory was sacrosanct among them, and to whom the promise regarding Christ had preceded. Conversely, because Luke wrote his Gospel for the Gentiles, he extends the line of genealogy from Adam all the way to God himself; so that they might understand that Christ’s grace pertains not to the Jews alone, but to the entire race of mortals. Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407), an influential Church Father famous for his preaching.</note> also pointed this out. Furthermore, he names David first: not only because the line of genealogy would be woven from the common repetition of both (the reason given by Saint Jerome), but also because his memory was more recent and more celebrated among the Hebrews, as Chrysostom suggests.
4 *Begat Isaac*] <note>original: "ἐγέννησε τὸν Ἰσαάκ"</note> The Greek Translator, whoever he was. For according to Jerome, it was once established that this Gospel was written by Matthew in Hebrew, which Chrysostom however does not dare to assert; but he says, "it is said," which although it may be established, I would rather it were still in existence than merely established. There are even those who think it was translated into the Greek language by John. Truly, as far as I can recall, Jerome nowhere clearly indicates that he himself saw the Gospel of Matthew written in Hebrew, especially since he professes to have corrected the four Gospels according to the "Greek truth," <note>Erasmus refers here to the *Graeca Veritas*, the principle that the Greek text is the ultimate authority for the New Testament.</note> and since he wrote commentaries on this one. Then there is the fact that in this Gospel quite a few things are cited from the books of the Old Testament which seem to differ from the original sources themselves. This occasion alone might have compelled Jerome to flee to the archetype of Matthew, especially since he is accustomed to do so in other places frequently for reasons not very serious. Furthermore, as to who translated it from the Hebrew speech into Greek, that is not known in any

way. That age was so free from all ambition. But as I began, whoever the Translator was, he diligently added his articles to the Hebrew names: so that since the words are foreign <note>original: "barbarica" - meaning non-Greek/Latin</note> and do not vary by any inflection of cases, the Reader could in this way distinguish gender and case: "to the Isaac," "from the Thamar" <note>original: "τῷ Ἰσαὰκ ἐκ τῆς Θάμαρ"</note>. Now, this might have seemed too trivial a point to mention, were we not now especially engaged in this business, that the Greek codices vary: in some "Iesaios" <note>original: "Ἰησαῖος"</note> is added, in most it is not "Iesaios" but "Iessaios" <note>original: "Ἰεσσαῖος" - Jesse</note>. Likewise, the Attics [Greeks] constantly add the letter 'n' whether a consonant or a vowel follows; the Ionians, on the contrary, do not. An example of this is in Aristophanes' *Plutus*: "and a prophet, as they say, wise" <note>original: "καὶ μάντις, ὡς φασιν, σοφός"</note>. <margin>C</margin> For if you read "phasi" [without the 'n'], the meter of the verse will not stand. An example of the latter is that of Homer: "they bore better men than the best men present." <note>original: "ἔτικτον ἀμείνονα, πρὸ κείμενων ἀρίστων"</note> And it is common among the Greeks to use "esti hote" for "enioi" [some]. Therefore, it is not a matter that should greatly disturb the Reader, whether he finds the 'n' added or otherwise. Even so, we have followed the common Greek language in this, adding the 'n' whenever a vowel follows, and omitting it whenever a consonant follows: especially since we saw that most Greek codices agree in this.

5 *From Thamar*] <note>original: "ἐκ τῆς Θάμαρ"</note> *From Rahab* <note>original: "ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ"</note>. It is strange why the Latin Translator [of the Vulgate] preferred the preposition "de" rather than "ex." For who is said to have begotten or received a son *de* [from] her, and not rather *ex* [out of] her? Not that I am unaware that "de" is found placed for "ex" in approved Authors. But I think it should be avoided, as it is like that Homeric phrase: and it would be foolish if anyone thought that what a Writer allowed himself in one or two places is permitted everywhere. For who would endure it if someone said, "I learned *de* [from/about] your letters," when in Latin we say, "I learned *ex* [out of/from] your letters." Furthermore, the Greeks, since they have no way to aspirate a vowel unless it is at the beginning of a word, express the Hebrew aspiration *Heth* (ח), as best they can, through *chi* (χ), thus <margin>D</margin> *Rachab*. And in the same way today the Jews pronounce it, just as they say the Spaniards pronounce that letter. Certainly, I found "Rachab" written in the library of the most illustrious Lady Margaret—a woman filled with every kind of virtue beyond the manner of her sex, and plainly worthy of both her father Maximilian, her brother Philip, and her grandsons Emperor Charles and Ferdinand: the former of whom the favor of the Divine Will has raised to such happiness that a greater happiness could hardly be wished for by a man; the latter is so adorned with all heroic and truly royal gifts that no fortune could happen so great as not to seem inferior to his true and proper virtues. And would that men would imitate the example of Margaret, and prefer to consume what free time is given from business in the reading of good volumes, than to waste it in games or empty stories. The manuscript is remarkable, written entirely in golden letters. It is kept at Mechelen <note>A city in present-day Belgium, then part of the Burgundian Netherlands.</note>, if anyone perhaps wishes to test my word. Jerome also indicated this somewhere. Theophylact <note>Theophylact of Ohrid, a Byzantine commentator mentioned in the previous page.</note> seems to doubt whether this was the Rahab who received the Hebrew spies at Jericho. For he speaks thus: "some think."

<margin>E</margin> 6 *David the king*] The Translator added the article "the king" <note>original: "τὸν βασιλέα"</note>, as if distinguishing him from some other David who was not a king, or doing this so that he may be understood here as a king of distinction: though he commemorates many other kings, yet he ascribes the honor of the royal surname to none. But soon when he repeats "David," he insists in the same way on the surname of king with the article prefixed, so that he might commend his recent and celebrated memory among the Jews with the honor of the title as well. Furthermore, if he added the article for the reason that this was the first king of all those who are reviewed in the genealogy, it was sufficient to add "king" [basilea] without the article.

7 *From her who was Uriah's*] <note>original: "ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου"</note> that is, from the wife of Uriah, or from her who had been the wife of Uriah. For in this kind of phrase, the Greek article performs the role of the noun which is understood. When, however, a little later he translates "the [son] of Zebedee" <note>original: "τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου"</note>: just as
