And God 4 shall wipe away every tear from their eyes: and death shall be no more, nor mourning, nor crying, nor pain shall be anymore, because the former things have passed away. And 5 he who sat on the throne said, Behold I make all things new. And he said to me, Write, because these words are faithful and true. And he said to me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the 6 beginning and the end. I will give to him who thirsts from the fountain of the water of life freely. He who overcomes shall possess all things, and I will be his God, 7 <margin>C</margin> and he shall be my son. But for the fearful, and unbelieving, 8 and the cursed, and murderers, and fornicators, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, their portion shall be in the pool burning with fire and sulfur, which is the second death. And there came to me one of the seven 9 angels having the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues, and he spoke with me, saying, Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the lamb. And he took me 10 in spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great holy city Jerusalem, descending from heaven from God, Having the brightness of God: and 11 its light was like a most precious stone, as it were a † jasper stone shining like crystal. And it had a wall great 12 and high, having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are the names <margin>D</margin> of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. From the east three 13 gates, from the north three gates, from the south three gates, from the west three gates. And the wall of the city having twelve 14 foundations, and in them the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the lamb. And he who spoke with me had 15 a golden reed measure, that he might measure the city, and its gates, and its wall. And the city 16 is set in a square, and its length is as great as its breadth, and he measured the city with the golden reed for twelve thousand stadia, and its length and height and breadth are equal. And he measured 17 its wall of one hundred and forty-four cubits, the measure of a man, which is of an angel. And the structure of its wall was of 18 <margin>E</margin> jasper: but the city itself was pure gold, like clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were adorned 19 with every precious stone: the first foundation jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, The fifth sardonyx, the sixth sardius, 20 the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh hyacinth, the twelfth amethyst. And the twelve gates 21 are twelve pearls, one for each, and the individual gates were of individual pearls, and the street of the city was pure gold like transparent glass. And a temple 22 <margin>F</margin> I did not see in it: for the Lord God Almighty is its temple, and the lamb. And the city does not need the sun, 23 nor the moon, to shine in it: for the brightness of God illuminated it, and its lamp is the lamb. And 24 the nations which were saved shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth shall bring their glory and honor into it, And its gates shall not be closed by day: for night 25 shall not be there. And they shall bring the glory and honor of the 26 nations...

# ->REVELATION CHAPTER XXII.<-

27 And there shall not enter into it anything common, or anything that practices abomination or falsehood, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

<margin>XXII.</margin>
1 And he showed me a pure river of the water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
2 In the middle of its street, and on either side of the river, was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit every month; and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
3 <margin>Otherwise "accursed thing"</margin> And there shall be no more any accursed thing <note>original: "κατάθεμα"; a thing devoted to destruction or a curse.</note>; but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it, and his servants shall serve him,
4 And they shall see his face, and his name shall be on their foreheads.
5 And there shall be no night there, and they have no need of a lamp or the light of the sun, for the Lord God enlightens them, and they shall reign forever and ever.
6 And he said to me, "These words are faithful and true. And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place."
7 "Behold, I am coming quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book."
8 And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who showed me these things.
9 And he says to me, "See that you do not do this; for I am your fellow servant, and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God."
10 And he says to me, "Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near."
11 Let the one who does wrong continue to do wrong, and let the filthy continue to be filthy; and let the righteous continue to be righteous, and the holy continue to be holy.
12 "And behold, I am coming quickly; and my reward is with me, to give to each according to his work."
13 "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last."
14 Blessed are those who do his commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter through the gates into the city.
15 But outside are the dogs, and the sorcerers, and the sexually immoral, and the murderers, and the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.
16 "I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you in the Churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, the bright and morning star."
17 And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come." And let him who hears say, "Come." And let him who thirsts come; and let him who desires take the water of life freely.
18 For I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues written in this book.
19 And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part from the book of life, and from the holy city, and from the things written in this book.
20 He who testifies to these things says, "Yes, I am coming quickly." Amen, yes, come, Lord Jesus.

27 <margin>A</margin> ...into it. Nothing that defiles shall enter it, or anything that works abomination and a lie, but only they who are written in the book of life of the lamb.

<margin>XXII.</margin>
1 And he showed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the seat of God and of the lamb.
2 In the middle of its street, and on both sides of the river was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit each month: and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.
3 And every curse shall be no more: but the seat of God and of the lamb shall be in it, and his servants shall serve him,
4 And they shall see his face, and his name on their foreheads.
5 <margin>B</margin> And night shall not be there, and they do not need the light of a lamp, nor the light of the sun, because the Lord God enlightens them, and they shall reign for ages of ages.
6 And he said to me, "These words are faithful and true. And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent his angel to show his servants what must happen quickly."
7 "And behold, I come swiftly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book."
8 And I am John who heard and saw these things. And after I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who showed me these things.
9 And he says to me, "See that you do not do it, for I am your fellow servant, and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep the words of the prophecy of this book. Adore God."
10 And he says to me, "Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book: for the time is near."
11 <margin>C</margin> He who harms, let him harm still, and he who is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he who is just, let him be justified still, and the holy be sanctified still.
12 "And behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to each as his work shall be."
13 "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end."
14 Blessed are they who keep his commandments, that their power may be in the tree of life, and they may enter through the gates into the city.
15 But outside are dogs, and sorcerers, and the unchaste, and murderers, and those serving idols, and everyone who loves and makes a lie.
16 "I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you in the Churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, the bright and morning star."
17 And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come." And let him who hears say, "Come." And let him who thirsts come: and let him who wills receive the water of life freely.
18 <margin>D</margin> For I contest to every one hearing the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone shall add to these, God will add upon him the plagues written in this book.
19 And if anyone shall diminish from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part from the book of life, and from the holy city, and from these things which are written in this book.
20 He who gives testimony of these things says, "Yes, I come quickly." Amen.

---

<margin>1</margin> *He who harms, let him harm*] <note>original: "Ὁ ἀδικῶν"</note>, that is, *the one who acts wickedly, or who is injurious*. And *still* <note>original: "adhuc"</note> is placed *for further*.

<margin>2</margin> *Blessed are those who wash their robes*] The Greeks have something quite different: <note>original: "Μακάριοι οἱ ποιοῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ"</note>, that is, *Blessed are those who do his commandments*. The translator seems to have read <note>original: "οἱ πλύνοντες τὰς στολάς"</note>. But from where does the following part come, *in the blood of the lamb*? For that is certainly not read among the Greeks at all.

<margin>3</margin> <margin>E</margin> *Even so, come quickly*] <note>original: "Ναὶ ἔρχομαι ταχύ"</note>. *Na* <note>original: "Ναὶ"</note> is for one confirming. But the same adverb is presently repeated by the Greeks, *Even so, come Lord Jesus*. Saint Jerome testifies that the Apocalypse was not even in his own age received by the Greeks. In addition to this, some very learned men attacked this whole subject as if it were a fiction with many insults, as if it had nothing of Apostolic gravity, but only shadowed forth common history under the coverings of figures. Furthermore, they say there is nothing in the sentiments that seems worthy of Apostolic majesty. To say nothing of these things for the moment, I would be moved somewhat by other conjectures, as well as by those facts: that in writing the revelations, he so solicitously insistently repeats his own name, *I John, I John*. It is as if he were writing a legal contract <note>term: "syngrapham" - a formal written obligation or bond</note>, not a book. And this is not only contrary to the custom of the other Apostles, but much more contrary to his own custom, who, when narrating in the Gospel, never expresses his own name anywhere, but indicates it by markers, *that disciple whom Jesus loved*. And Paul, when compelled, says *I John*. Furthermore, in the Greek codices I have seen, the title was not *of John the Evangelist, but of John the Theologian*, not to mention a style that is quite dissonant from that which is in the Gospel and the Epistle. For concerning the passages which some have slandered as smelling of the dogmas of heretics, it would not be a matter of great difficulty to clear them. These things, I say, would move me somewhat to less believe it to be by John the Evangelist, unless the consensus of the world called me elsewhere, and especially the authority of the Church—if indeed the Church approves this work with this mind, that it wishes it to be held as John the Evangelist's, and to be of equal weight with the other canonical books. Now Dorotheus, Bishop of Tyre and Martyr, in his summary of lives, handed down that John the Evangelist wrote his work on the island of Patmos. Also—

<column-break/>

<margin>F</margin> —Eusebius <note>A 4th-century church historian</note> records that it was written at Ephesus. However, he makes no mention of the Apocalypse at all. Not even Anastasius the Greek, in his catalog, dares to affirm that this work is his; he only says it was received by some as if it were his work. Dionysius, Bishop of Alexandria <note>A 3rd-century theologian</note>, who seems to have felt most candidly about this work, differs indeed from those who judged it to belong to Cerinthus the heretic. Cerinthus’s dogma was that there would one day be a kingdom of Christ on earth, and then whatever pleasures had been despised for Christ’s sake would return with abundant interest—wealth would return, sacrifices and feast days of the Mosaic Law would return. And they say with this purpose he prefixed the title *of John the Apostle* to another's work, so that he might commend his own errors, mixed into this book, to the simple-minded under the pretense of an Apostolic name. Nevertheless, Dionysius suspects the book was written by some other holy man named John, and many Christians were of this opinion, by whose judgment he was moved and did not dare to reject the book. Furthermore, as to why he suspects the work is not that of *John the Apostle*, who was the son of Zebedee and brother of James, he brings forward no other cause except the one we also reviewed, namely, that he repeatedly insists upon his own name. These things and several others concerning this book are reviewed by Eusebius of Caesarea in the *seventh book of his Ecclesiastical History*. Likewise, in the third book, making mention of this work, he says, *in the Revelation which is called John’s*. Again, a little later, among the books of the New Testament about which there was once doubt, he lists the *Revelation of John*, the *Epistle of James and Jude, and the second of Peter, and the second and third of John*. Again, a little later in the same book, he cites a certain orthodox author named Caius, who does not hesitate to attribute this work to Cerinthus the heretic, showing in many words what poisons of his heresy he mixed into this book, meanwhile abusing the authority of the Apostolic name. For my part, when I look at the malicious arts of the heretics, I could easily be led to believe that Cerinthus, who lived in the age of John and, I believe, survived him, wished to spread his virus into the world by this fabrication. But again, it is impossible to be persuaded that God would have allowed the Devil's trick to delude the Christian people with impunity for so many centuries. For it is certain that this work is very ancient, seeing that the very ancient Irenaeus, and Justin Martyr, older than him, deemed it worthy of their commentaries. Although Irenaeus, according to Eusebius in the third book, besides the Apostles, to whom he joins John the Evangelist, commemorates a certain Aristion and—

...and John the elder <note>original: "Joannem presbyterum"; Erasmus is distinguishing between John the Apostle and another "John the Elder" mentioned by early church historians</note>, whom Eusebius suspects is the author of the Revelation. For Jerome testifies that the two later Epistles are ascribed to this same man. Jerome also testifies in his Letter to Dardanus that in his time, the Letter to the Hebrews was commonly rejected in scholarly disputes by the Latins, and similarly the Revelation was rejected by the Greeks. Nevertheless, the ancient writers drew testimonies from both works. Furthermore, in more than one place, Jerome commends this work against the rejection of the Greeks. Again, when explaining the 36th chapter of Ezekiel, he admits that Irenaeus was not entirely averse to the opinion of the Chiliasts <note>original: "Chiliastarum"; from the Greek word for "one thousand," referring to the Millenarians who believed in a literal 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ</note>, just as Tertullian, Lactantius, Victorinus, and Apollinaris were not. For Cerinthus <note>A gnostic heretic who was a contemporary of the Apostle John</note> taught that Christ had not

<column-break/>

21 Amen, yes, come Lord Jesus. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

->THE REVELATION OF JOHN<-

->T H E   E N D .<-

yet risen, but was to rise again, and after a thousand years would reign on the earth with his followers in an incredible happiness of all things. Indeed, mention is frequently made of the Millenarians here, as in chapters 12 and 20. This book is not as effective for proving points of doctrine, since it consists entirely of allegories, but it contributes a great deal to understanding the origins of the Church. Even among gems there is some distinction, and some gold is purer and more proven than other gold. In sacred matters as well, one thing is more sacred than another. He who is spiritual, as Paul says, judges all things, and is judged by no one.

# ILLUSTRATION: DECORATIVE ENDPAPER

->[Full-page illustration]<-

This page consists of a full-page **marbled paper** pattern, a decorative technique frequently employed in high-quality bookbinding for **endpapers** <note>The sheets of paper pasted to the inner covers of a book to hide the binding construction and provide a decorative finish.</note>.

The pattern shown here is known as a **nonpareil pattern** <note>From the French for "unrivaled," this is a traditional marbling design created by dragging a fine-toothed comb through pigments floating on a liquid surface.</note>. It is characterized by its dense, repeating rows of small scalloped and wave-like shapes that create a rhythmic visual flow across the entire surface.

The artisan utilized a specific color palette consisting of:
*   **Dark red**
*   **Light blue**
*   **Ochre yellow**
*   **White**

These colors are interlaced in fine, alternating lines, resulting in a vibrant and highly textured appearance. Such papers were not only prized for their beauty but also served a practical purpose, as the complex patterns helped to disguise any stains or wear that the inside of the book cover might acquire over centuries of use.

<summary>A full-page illustration of a marbled paper endpaper featuring a rhythmic nonpareil pattern. The design uses a palette of dark red, light blue, ochre yellow, and white to create a decorative finish for the manuscript binding.</summary>
<keywords>marbled paper, nonpareil pattern, bookbinding, endpaper, decorative arts, Renaissance binding</keywords>
